FAQ
Pricing FAQStill have questions? Book a demo→See all frequently asked questions →
How does Numeo pricing work?
Each product is priced for who uses it. Numeo Spot, Load Hub, Load Radar, and AI Hub are priced per dispatcher seat (Spot Free, Pro $9.99/mo annual, Ultra $29.99/mo annual). Numeo One TMS is priced per fleet by truck count. Pick the product that matches your biggest pain first, then choose the tier that fits your size.
Which plan is right for a small carrier?
If finding loads is the bottleneck, start with the free Spot extension or Load Hub (in Ultra). If broker emails and follow-ups eat the day, AI Hub (in Ultra) helps. If you're outgrowing spreadsheets and want dispatch, accounting, and compliance in one place, Numeo One Basic starts at a $99/month minimum through 10 trucks. Many small carriers run Spot Ultra and Numeo One together.
How much is Numeo One for my fleet size?
Numeo One has a $99/month Basic minimum and $149/month Pro minimum through 10 trucks, with overage beyond the cap and 30% off annual billing. Larger fleets use the current overage formula or custom Enterprise pricing. Plan inclusions differ by tier, so confirm the current feature matrix on the pricing page.
Do I still pay for DAT or Truckstop separately?
Yes. Numeo works on top of the load boards you already subscribe to — you bring your credentials and Numeo adds AI on top. The same applies to ELDs, factoring partners, and broker portals: you keep those accounts and Numeo connects to them. Numeo One is the only product that can stand alone as a full system.
Is Numeo priced per truck, per user, or per seat?
It depends on the product. Spot, Load Hub, Load Radar, and AI Hub are per dispatcher seat. Numeo One TMS starts at a $99/month Basic minimum and $149/month Pro minimum for up to 10 trucks, with overage beyond the cap and custom Enterprise pricing for larger fleets. Confirm the current plan details on the pricing page.
Is there a free trial or free plan?
Both. Numeo Spot is free forever for solo dispatchers (no card). Spot Pro and Numeo One (TMS) include a 14-day free trial, also no card. Spot Ultra has no separate trial — you subscribe directly — but it includes 3 months of Numeo One so you can try the full TMS before committing to a fleet plan.
Can Numeo replace my current TMS to save money?
Often, yes. Numeo One is an AI-native TMS with a $99/month Basic minimum for up to 10 trucks, while traditional systems like McLeod or Turvo typically require a quote. Carriers on spreadsheets or light tools may replace them; carriers on a heavier TMS can layer Numeo’s dispatch automation on top. The right answer depends on your current setup.
What's the fastest way to get started?
Install the free Numeo Spot Chrome extension and try it inside your existing DAT or Truckstop tab — no setup needed. To see the full platform or plan a larger-fleet rollout, book a demo and the team walks through it with your trucks, lanes, and current tools in mind.

What is the best AI dispatch tool for carriers in 2026?
The best AI dispatch tool depends on the carrier's boards, TMS, approval policy, and communication workflow. Numeo is designed for teams that want load finding, email-based rate negotiation, and broker updates layered onto DAT, Truckstop, and an existing TMS. It has a free plan; paid pricing starts at $9.99/dispatcher/mo annually, subject to current plan terms.
How is an AI dispatch tool different from a load board?
A load board (DAT, Truckstop) shows you postings; an AI dispatch tool does the work around them. Numeo ranks those postings by profit for your truck, drafts the broker negotiation email, uses booking context from your history, and keeps brokers updated automatically — turning the board from a list into a worked queue. A published Four Ways Cargo story describes this workflow in a 150-truck operation; no numeric customer outcome is presented here as a benchmark.
Who gets the most value from AI dispatch software?
Dispatchers working at carriers (not 3PLs) gain the most. A typical dispatch day is 10–12 hours, of which only 1–2 are the booking work that actually pays — the rest is load search, rate negotiation, check calls, email, and paperwork. AI dispatch automates enough of that to let one dispatcher cover more trucks without longer hours.
What's the best AI Chrome extension for DAT?
Numeo Spot. It adds AI load ranking, inline broker factoring/safety checks, one-click rate-negotiation emails, and automatic status updates inside DAT (and Truckstop). It's free to install from the Chrome Web Store and works on every DAT tier — the fastest way to add AI to a board you already pay for.
What's the best AI TMS for small and mid-size carriers?
Numeo One — an AI-native TMS starting at a $99/month minimum on Basic and $149/month minimum on Pro through 10 trucks, well under traditional platforms like McLeod or Turvo (~$290–$410+/user/mo). Carriers already on a TMS typically run Numeo's load tools on top as the AI automation layer.
What should I look for when comparing AI dispatch tools?
Check whether it works on top of your boards or forces a migration, whether negotiation is automated (and on what channel), whether you keep an approval step, what it integrates with (DAT, Truckstop, your ELD and factoring), and whether pricing is published. Numeo is transparent on all five: layers on top, email negotiation, human approval by default, 35 source-listed integrations, public pricing.
How much does AI dispatch software cost?
Numeo starts free (Spot). Paid plans are $9.99/dispatcher/mo (Pro, annual) and $29.99/dispatcher/mo (Ultra, annual, which bundles Load Hub, Load Radar, AI Hub, and 3 months of Numeo One). Numeo One starts at a $99/month minimum on Basic and $149/month minimum on Pro through 10 trucks. Compared with a $56k–$91k/year W-2 dispatcher or a 5–10%-of-gross dispatch service, AI dispatch is a fraction of the entry cost.

What is Numeo Load Hub?
Load Hub is a single search workspace that pulls loads from 15+ brokerage portals, public boards, and aggregators into one window. Instead of tabbing between DAT, Truckstop, RXO, C.H. Robinson, J.B. Hunt, and Arrive, you run one search and see every source ranked by profit for your truck — with fuel cost and net profit shown before you click. It's bundled in Spot Ultra.
Do I have to cancel my existing load-board subscriptions?
No. Load Hub connects to the accounts you already have — you authenticate with your own DAT, Truckstop, or broker credentials and Load Hub mirrors that access into one search. You keep your subscriptions and your rates; Load Hub just aggregates them.
Which load boards and brokers does Load Hub search?
The connector menu spans 20+ sources, including TQL, C.H. Robinson, Arrive Logistics, RXO, Echo, Emerge, Spot Freight, J.B. Hunt, Knight-Swift, Schneider, Uber Freight, Convoy, Mode Global, Nolan, Sylectus, DAT, and Truckstop. New integrations are added on request, and you can ask the team to connect a broker or board that isn't listed yet.
Do I need an account with every broker Load Hub connects to?
For most sources, yes — you bring your own subscription and authenticate inside Numeo. Three sources need no prior subscription: Parade, HappyRobot, and TruckStop Trial. That lets you start aggregating immediately even before you've added every paid account.
How is Load Hub different from a load board like DAT?
DAT is one source; Load Hub searches DAT plus 14+ others at once. A board shows you its own postings in post order — Load Hub unifies many boards and brokerages into one filter set and ranks the combined results by profitability, with deadhead and fuel cost factored in before you open a load.
What filters can I use in Load Hub?
Filter by equipment (dry van, reefer, flatbed), lane, rate minimum ($/mile or total), distance, deadhead tolerance, and weight — set once and applied across every connected source. Recent searches are saved, and Load Radar can watch any saved search for new matches.
What does Load Hub cost?
Load Hub has no standalone price — it's bundled into Spot Ultra ($29.99/dispatcher/mo annual or $49.99 monthly), alongside Load Radar, AI Hub, and 3 months of Numeo One. Spot Free and Pro include a 30-search preview so you can try it first. Spot Pro includes a 14-day free trial; Ultra you subscribe to directly.
Does Load Hub include real-time alerts?
Yes — Load Radar is built in. In Load Hub it scans every connected source (not just DAT) and can push a notification when a matching load appears, via email, the Numeo App, and Telegram. On Spot Ultra those alerts are unlimited.

Questions about AI Hub.
How AI Hub finds, ranks, and negotiates loads — and where the dispatcher stays in control.Still have questions? Book a demo→See all frequently asked questions →
What is AI Hub?
AI Hub is Numeo's AI agent for the load-finding and booking workflow. It watches every connected load board, ranks the top matches against your dispatcher rules, and negotiates rates with brokers by email. It's bundled inside Spot Ultra, with a 15-search preview on Free and Pro.
How does AI Hub decide which loads to surface?
Your dispatcher rules are the only filter — equipment, lane, RPM floor, deadhead tolerance, broker score, and driver fit. AI Hub ranks loads strictly within those rules and never surfaces freight outside them. You can change the rules or override any recommendation at any time.
How does AI Hub communicate with brokers?
AI Hub handles broker negotiation through email. You can search in plain English, and the agent drafts and sends market-backed negotiation emails on your behalf while keeping the workflow reviewable.
Do I still approve loads, or does the AI book on its own?
You stay in control of booking decisions. AI Hub surfaces loads, prepares market-backed negotiation emails, and keeps the workflow reviewable; you approve any binding booking commitment before it ships.
Does AI Hub work without a TMS?
Yes. AI Hub runs on top of any setup — DAT alone, your existing TMS (Alvys, Rose Rocket, McLeod), or Numeo One. Connecting a TMS lets it learn from real driver behavior, lane history, and acceptance rate over time, but it's optional; without one, it uses the rules you set.
Can one person manage multiple MCs in AI Hub?
Yes. A single user can run multiple MCs from one seat, and AI Hub keeps email signatures, broker relationships, and per-MC rules separate. Spot Ultra supports up to 5 MC connections, so dispatching companies can centralize several carrier clients in one place.

What is the best DAT extension in 2026?
The right DAT add-on depends on the dispatcher's workflow. Numeo Spot is designed for dispatchers and owner-operators who want AI load ranking by profitability, inline broker factoring and safety checks, one-click rate-negotiation email drafts, profit and toll calculations, and broker status updates inside DAT and Truckstop. It's free to install from the Chrome Web Store.
Is the Numeo DAT extension free?
Yes. Numeo Spot is free to install and use alongside any DAT subscription. The free plan covers 20 one-click emails a day, 100 factoring checks, the calculators, and route view. Unlimited emails and team features start at $9.99/dispatcher/mo annual on Pro. Load Radar alerts and multi-board search via Load Hub are bundled into Ultra at $29.99/dispatcher/mo annual, with a preview on Free and Pro.
Does it work with DAT Power, DAT Pro, and DAT One?
Yes — Spot works on top of every DAT tier (DAT One, DAT Power, DAT Pro, DAT Enterprise). It doesn't replace DAT or require a specific plan; it layers AI ranking and automation onto the DAT interface you already use, the next time you open the tab.
How do I install the Numeo DAT extension?
Find "Numeo Spot" in the Chrome Web Store, click Add to Chrome, sign in with a free Numeo account (or create one), then refresh your DAT tab. The Numeo panel appears inside DAT automatically, with no platform migration required.
What does Numeo Spot do that DAT alone doesn't?
Five things DAT doesn't: (1) ranks loads by profit for your truck instead of newest-first, (2) shows broker factoring/safety status inline on each load, (3) drafts a market-backed rate-negotiation email in one click, (4) updates brokers on load status automatically, and (5) alerts your phone and Telegram via Load Radar when a matching load posts.

Install Spot (free), turn on AI ranking so your search sorts by profitability instead of post time, and enable Load Radar (Pro/Ultra) so matching loads can push to your phone and Telegram when they post. Radar helps you review matching DAT freight without relying on manual tab-by-tab checks.

Numeo App FAQStill have questions? Book a demo→See all frequently asked questions →
What is the Numeo App?
The Numeo App is a free iOS and Android app for owner-operators, company drivers and dispatchers. It brings a large aggregated load feed into one place. Set your pickup, trailer and date, look through what matches, check the broker and the market rate, and send the offer — or book the load yourself.
Is the Numeo App free?
Yes. Downloading it is free, searching is free, and AI Dispatch is free and unlimited on every plan including Free. The Go, Max and Platinum plans raise the search limit and open full detail on Amazon loads.
Does the app book loads for me?
It doesn't book anything on its own. You can book a load yourself in the app, and the app will write and send the offer email to the broker for you — but nothing is committed without you doing it.
What is AI Dispatch, and does it cost extra?
It's load search in plain language: describe the run you want and it returns its top three matches with the reasoning behind each one. You can push back, change your criteria mid-search, or ask for a human dispatcher. It's free and unlimited for every user — there's no tier for it.
How does the app check a broker?
You pick your factoring company in your profile, and every load then shows whether that broker clears with them. RTS, Triumph, WEX and Engaged Financial are among those supported. You can also block a broker or log an issue against one without leaving the load.
Where do the loads come from?
Truckstop, Parade and HappyRobot are connected by default, and you can link the board accounts you already pay for so their loads land in the same feed.
Can I use the app for Amazon loads?
Yes, and only in the app. Amazon has its own flow with Amazon's trailer list, the work opportunity type (run, trip or one-way), and the stop count. Full detail on Amazon loads is on the paid plans.
How is it different from a dispatch service?
A dispatch service takes a cut of every load you run and decides what you haul. The app does the searching, the broker checking and the offer writing, and leaves the decision — and the money — with you.

What is Numeo One?
Numeo One is an AI-native Transportation Management System for trucking carriers. Four modules — Operations & Dispatch, Accounting & Payments, Fleet Management, and Safety & Compliance — run in one platform with seven back-office AI agents handling the repetitive dispatch, paperwork, and follow-up work underneath. It's a full TMS, not an add-on layer.
Which AI agents are inside Numeo One, and what do they do?
Seven agents ship on every plan: Track & Trace (auto-updates brokers on pickup/transit/delivery and flags delays early), Document Abstraction (reads BOLs/PODs and validates them against the rate con), Accounting & Payments (chases invoices and classifies expenses), Fleet Management (monitors utilization, fuel, and maintenance), Rate Confirmation Reader (pulls rate cons from your inbox), POD & Rate Con Match, and Broker Email Responder. The Updater Assistant also sends scheduled status updates with live GPS and ETAs.
How is Numeo One priced?
Numeo One uses a monthly minimum through 10 trucks, with overage beyond the cap. Basic starts at $99/month and Pro at $149/month; annual billing currently saves 30%. Enterprise is custom for larger fleets, with volume pricing, a dedicated CSM, SSO, and custom integrations.
What does Numeo One integrate with?
35 source-listed integrations across five categories: 21 ELDs (Samsara, Motive, Lucid ELD and more), 7 factoring partners (RTS, Triumph, PRO Funding, WEX, Stratopay, Outgo, TAFS), 3 toll/fuel systems (BestPass, Relay Payments, PrePass), 3 account and accounting connectors for running alongside another TMS (DITAT, QuickManage, QuickBooks Online), and 1 trailer-GPS provider (Phillips Connect) — plus Gmail/Outlook via OAuth. It drops into your existing stack, no rip-and-replace.
Does Numeo One replace my existing TMS?
It can. Carriers on spreadsheets or lightweight tools usually migrate fully. Carriers on a heavier system (McLeod, Turvo, Reefer TMS) often run Numeo One alongside it using account-level sync (DITAT, QuickManage) — Numeo handles AI-assisted broker email workflows, document abstraction, and accounting automation while the legacy system keeps its role. Migration timing depends on the carrier's data, integrations, and rollout scope.
How is Numeo One different from AI Hub?
They're two products for two halves of the day. AI Hub is the front-office agent for finding, ranking, and booking loads (by email), bundled in Spot Ultra. Numeo One is the back-office TMS that runs everything after the load is booked — dispatch, tracking, paperwork, accounting, and compliance — with its own seven AI agents. Use either alone or both together.
Is every feature included, or are there feature tiers?
Every Numeo One plan includes every module and every AI agent — pricing scales with fleet size only, never by feature. There are no locked modules on Basic and no premium upsell tiers; an 8-truck carrier and a 24-truck carrier get the same capabilities.
How long does Numeo One take to set up?
Numeo supports hands-on onboarding — connecting load boards, importing driver and broker contacts, and configuring the AI agents for your most-run lanes. Larger fleets can receive migration support from their current TMS. The rollout plan and timing depend on the fleet's setup and integration scope. Spot Ultra also includes 3 months of Numeo One to trial it.

What is the best TMS for a small trucking company?
It depends which problem you are solving. If you need cheap, predictable record-keeping above about 10 trucks, TruckingOffice publishes a flat $90/month Basic tier that is hard to beat on price. If dispatcher hours are the constraint — someone working load boards and broker email all day — Numeo One is built for that and starts at a $99/month minimum for up to 10 trucks. Truckbase is the stronger modern system of record once you are past roughly 25 trucks.
How much should a small carrier pay for a TMS?
Published rates for carriers under 25 trucks run from about $25/month flat to $290/month minimum, and several vendors publish nothing at all. A 10-truck fleet can reasonably expect $90–$150/month. Be wary of any comparison quoting a specific price for a vendor that does not publish one.
Is there a free TMS for small carriers?
AscendTMS has historically been the free-tier option in this category, though its pricing page now renders client-side so it cannot be verified without visiting directly. Numeo Spot is free permanently — it is a Chrome extension rather than a full TMS, but it is a way to test load search and broker negotiation without paying anything.
Do I need a TMS or just better dispatch tools?
A useful test: if your problem is that you cannot find the load or the invoice, you need a TMS. If your problem is that finding and negotiating the freight eats the day, a system of record will not fix it — that is a dispatch-automation problem. Buyer’s guide · Updated September 2026
What is the best truck dispatch software?
“Truck dispatch software” describes four different kinds of product that solve four different problems, from free tools to a $2,080-a-month platform. This page explains the difference and publishes what each one costs.
Start free See Numeo pricing →
Quick answer
What is truck dispatch software?
Truck dispatch software is the system a carrier uses to find freight, assign it to drivers, and handle the paperwork that follows. In practice the category splits four ways: load boards that only show available freight, a TMS that records and bills the work, an AI dispatch layer that does the searching and broker negotiation, and outsourced dispatch agencies that charge 5–10% of gross. Most carriers under 100 trucks end up running two of the four. Prices range from a $99 monthly minimum through 10 trucks to over $2,000 a month.
Best forCarriers deciding whether they need a load board, TMS, AI dispatch layer, or people.
Not best forBuyers looking for one universal product without checking fleet size, workflow, and pricing model.
EvidenceNumeo pricing
Last verifiedSeptember 2, 2026

The four kinds of truck dispatch software
Most buying mistakes in this category come from comparing two products that were never solving the same problem. Sort the shortlist by kind first.
Load boards
A marketplace of available freight. It shows you what is out there and stops. No paperwork, no settlements, no record of what you booked last month.
Best for: Owner-operators finding their own freight.
Transportation management systems (TMS)
The system of record. Loads, drivers, invoicing, settlements, IFTA, compliance. It organises the work but does not go and find it — you still search the boards and email the brokers yourself.
Best for: Fleets that have outgrown a spreadsheet.
AI dispatch layers
Software that does the searching and the broker outreach: ranking loads by what they are worth for a specific truck, drafting the rate email, following up. Sits on top of the boards and the TMS rather than replacing either.
Best for: Dispatchers whose day is search, email and follow-up.
Outsourced dispatch services
Not software — people. A dispatch agency takes a percentage of gross, typically 5–10%, and books on your behalf. Cheaper than software at one truck, far more expensive at ten.
Best for: Drivers who would rather not dispatch at all.
What truck dispatch software actually costs

Note how the pricing is expressed, not just the number. Per-user pricing punishes you for adding dispatchers; per-truck pricing scales with the thing that actually earns. A $69-per-user TMS is cheaper than a $299-per-month Pro minimum at twenty trucks — and far more expensive the other way round.
How to choose, in five questions
Where does the dispatcher’s day actually go? If it is searching and emailing, a TMS will not help — it records work rather than doing it.
Is the price per truck, per user, or per load? Model it at the fleet size you expect in a year, not the one you have today.
Does it run where you already work? Software that lives in a separate tab gets abandoned; software inside DAT or Truckstop does not.
What happens after the load is booked? Invoicing, settlements, IFTA and compliance are where the hours quietly go.
Can you leave? Check contract length and whether your load history exports.

Truck dispatch software is the system a carrier uses to find freight, assign it to drivers, and handle the paperwork that follows. The category splits four ways: load boards that show available freight, a TMS that records and bills the work, an AI dispatch layer that does the searching and broker negotiation, and outsourced dispatch agencies charging 5–10% of gross. How much does truck dispatch software cost?

What is the difference between a TMS and dispatch software?
A TMS is the system of record — it organises loads, drivers, invoicing, settlements, IFTA and compliance, but it does not go and find freight. Dispatch software in the working sense does the finding: searching boards, ranking loads by profit for a specific truck, and handling broker outreach. Carriers frequently need both, which is why AI dispatch layers are built to sit on top of an existing TMS rather than replace it.
Is per-truck or per-user pricing better?
It depends on your shape. Numeo One uses a monthly minimum through 10 trucks and an overage formula after the cap, while other TMS products may price per user, truck, load, or flat tier. Model each option at the fleet size and dispatcher count you expect in a year, then compare what the price includes.
Do I need dispatch software for one truck?
Not necessarily software you pay for. At one truck the free tier of a load board app usually covers it, and an outsourced dispatch service taking 5–10% of gross is the common alternative. Paid dispatch software starts to pay for itself when a dispatcher's time becomes the constraint — typically somewhere between three and five trucks, or when the paperwork after booking starts eating evenings.

The honest read: if all you want is to look at loads, Trucker Path is the least restricted free board and TruckSmarter is the most established. What none of the free tiers do is the work after you find the load — pulling the broker’s credit, drafting the rate email, following up. That is the part every board charges for, and it is the part that decides whether a free board saves you money or just saves you a subscription.
What the free Numeo app includes — and where it stops
We would rather you read the limit here than discover it later. The Numeo app is free to download and free to keep using:
Large aggregated load feed, searchable by equipment, lane, rate, mileage and deadhead

Where it stops: the Go, Max and Platinum plans raise the search limit and open full detail on Amazon loads. That is the whole difference on mobile — AI Dispatch is not one of the things you pay for. The app also never books on its own; you book, and it writes the outreach. On the desktop side, Load Hub searches 15+ boards and broker portals in one window, Load Radar sends phone and Telegram alerts when a matching load posts, and AI Hub handles broker email at volume. Those three are bundled into Numeo Spot Ultra — $29.99 per dispatcher per month billed annually, $49.99 monthly — and Spot Free and Pro include a 30-search preview so you can try them first. Full detail on pricing.
Free load boards by equipment type
The board matters less than the filter. What separates a good free board from a bad one is whether it can express what your truck actually hauls.
Box truck
Box-truck freight is the hardest category to find on a general board, because most boards treat it as an afterthought behind dry van. Filter by straight truck and 26ft box, and watch for loads posted as "van" that a box truck cannot legally take — no dock, no liftgate, no pallet jack.
Hotshot
Hotshot runs on Class 3–5 trucks with gooseneck or flatbed trailers, usually under 10,000 lbs. The freight moves fast and prices on urgency, so the boards that refresh quickest matter more than the boards with the most postings.
Flatbed
Flatbed rates swing harder by season and region than any other equipment type. Steel, lumber and machinery concentrate around a handful of origins, so a board that lets you search by origin radius rather than by state is worth more than raw posting volume.
Reefer
Reefer pays a premium and demands more: temperature logs, tighter appointment windows, and more detention risk. Check the broker before the rate — a good reefer rate from a slow-paying broker is not a good load.
Power only
Power only means you pull someone else’s trailer, which removes the trailer payment but ties you to that shipper’s network. Volumes are thinner on free boards because much of it moves through dedicated programs rather than open postings.

Numeo products support broker and operations workflows by email. The AI Dispatch mobile app also includes voice mode, so drivers and dispatchers can interact with the assistant hands-free while working from a phone.

TruckSmarter's app and board are free too, though its AI Dispatch is $49/month after a 30-day trial. What is the catch with a free load board?
Usually one of three things: the free tier caps how many loads you can see (DAT), it is a trial rather than a free plan (123Loadboard), or the board is free but the tools that make it useful are not (TruckSmarter charges $49/month for AI dispatch). The Numeo app is only partly the first kind: search is free up to the free plan's limit, but AI Dispatch and AI load ranking are free and unlimited on every plan including Free — the paid plans buy a higher search limit and full Amazon load detail, not the AI.
Is the Numeo load board free forever?
The app is free to download and free to keep using, with a large aggregated load feed in one place. AI Dispatch and AI load ranking are free and unlimited on every plan, including Free — no tier, no monthly cap, no add-on. The Go, Max and Platinum plans raise the search limit and open full detail on Amazon loads, which are in the Numeo app and nowhere else. Do free load boards have real loads or leftovers?
Both, and the mix depends on the board's source. Boards that aggregate broker postings carry the same freight the paid boards do, because brokers post to fill trucks rather than to fill tiers. What a paid subscription usually buys is not better freight but better search: rate history on the lane, broker credit and days-to-pay, and alerts that reach you before the load is covered.
What is the best free load board for box trucks?
Box-truck freight is filtered rather than found — most general boards bury straight-truck and 26ft box loads behind dry van, and some loads posted as "van" cannot legally be taken by a box truck without a dock, liftgate or pallet jack. Pick a board that lets you filter by straight truck and box specifically. The Numeo app filters by equipment, lane, rate, mileage and deadhead on the free tier.

Unlike a load board that only shows freight, Numeo automates the work around finding, negotiating, and preparing a booking — without ripping out your current stack.
What does Numeo actually do for a dispatcher?
Numeo handles the repetitive parts of dispatch so you book more loads in fewer hours: it searches every connected board at once, ranks loads by profit for your truck, drafts market-backed negotiation emails, and keeps brokers updated on status automatically. The dispatcher still chooses the load — Numeo removes the copy-paste, tab-switching, and follow-up.
What is the best Chrome extension for DAT and Truckstop?
The right DAT or Truckstop extension depends on whether you need ranking, broker checks, negotiation drafts, or alerts. Numeo Spot is a fit for dispatchers who want those tools inside the board they already use. It is free to install; current limits, ratings, and compatibility should be verified in the Chrome Web Store listing and on the Spot page.
What is the best TMS for small carriers?
Numeo One starts at a $99/month minimum on Basic and $149/month minimum on Pro for up to 10 trucks, with overage beyond the cap — far cheaper at entry than traditional systems like McLeod or Turvo, which often require a quote. Every plan includes the core dispatch, accounting, fleet, and safety foundation; confirm current AI and plan details on the pricing page.
What is the fastest way to find loads?
Search every board at once instead of tab-by-tab. Numeo Load Hub queries 15+ load boards and broker portals (RXO, C.H. Robinson, Arrive, TQL, J.B. Hunt, Echo, Schneider and more) in one search, ranked by profit for your truck. Turn on Load Radar and matching loads can push to your phone and Telegram when they are found, helping reduce manual search delay.
How do I find loads fast on DAT specifically?
Install the free Numeo Spot extension on top of DAT. It re-ranks your search by profitability instead of post time, shows broker safety/factoring status inline, and drafts a rate-negotiation email in one click. Add Load Radar (Pro/Ultra) so matching DAT loads alert your phone and Telegram shortly after they post.
Does Numeo replace my DAT, Truckstop, or TMS subscription?
No. Numeo Spot, Load Hub, and AI Hub sit on top of the boards and broker portals you already pay for — you bring your own credentials and keep your accounts. Numeo One is the exception: it's a full TMS that can replace a legacy system or run alongside it via account-level sync (DITAT, QuickManage).
Is Numeo secure with my email and account data?
Yes. Numeo maintains SOC 2 Type II certification (our email infrastructure provider is additionally ISO 27001 certified), connects email through OAuth 2.0 (passwords are never stored), and encrypts data at rest with AES-256 and in transit. Email access is limited to sending broker emails and reading load/broker messages — never resold, never used for ads.
How much does Numeo cost?
Numeo Spot is free for solo dispatchers. Spot Pro is $9.99/dispatcher/mo annual ($14.99 monthly); Spot Ultra is $29.99/dispatcher/mo annual ($49.99 monthly) and bundles Load Hub, Load Radar, AI Hub, and 3 months of Numeo One. Numeo One starts at a $99/month minimum on Basic and $149/month minimum on Pro for up to 10 trucks, with custom Enterprise pricing for larger fleets. See numeo.ai/pricing.

Trucking companies by state
Top trucking companies, by US state
Top trucking companies, brokers, and 3PLs in each state, plus freight-market overviews, regulatory notes, and load-finding playbooks for 20 top freight states.
TX
Texas trucking companies
Texas is the largest US freight state by truck volume — Dallas, Houston, and the Laredo border crossing combine for an estimated 15–18% of all US truckload originations. Year-round consistent volume, strong reefer share, and the highest cross-border freight density in the country.See Texas guide 
CA
California trucking companies
California is the #2 US freight state and the largest inbound freight market in the country. The LA/Long Beach port complex drives roughly 40% of US containerized inbound freight. Strict emissions regulations (CARB) shape equipment standards statewide.See California guide 
FL
Florida trucking companies
Florida is the Southeast’s largest inbound freight state, anchored by the Port of Jacksonville and dense reefer flow from Miami’s Latin American produce trade. Heavy tourism-driven consumer-goods inbound creates consistent demand.See Florida guide 
IL
Illinois trucking companies
Illinois — anchored by Chicago — is the highest-density freight state in the Midwest. Roughly 20% of long-haul truckload originations cross the Chicago metro weekly. Strong manufacturer and rail-to-truck crossdock volume.See Illinois guide 
GA
Georgia trucking companies
Georgia is the Southeast freight capital. Atlanta is one of the top-5 US freight origin metros and the Port of Savannah is the second-busiest US container port by some measures. Heavy dry van and reefer volume.See Georgia guide 
TN
Tennessee trucking companies
Tennessee is one of the fastest-growing freight states, anchored by FedEx Memphis (the largest parcel-to-truckload conversion hub in the US) and Nashville’s booming automotive and distribution sector.See Tennessee guide 
NC
North Carolina trucking companies
North Carolina is the largest freight market in the Carolinas. Charlotte is the regional distribution hub and the Port of Wilmington adds steady containerized freight flow. Strong textiles, furniture, and tobacco legacy still drive specialty freight.See North Carolina guide 
OH
Ohio trucking companies
Ohio is one of the densest Midwest freight states — Columbus, Cincinnati, Cleveland, and Toledo together generate consistent year-round volume. Heavy auto-parts JIT freight, plus dense FedEx and Amazon air-cargo conversion.See Ohio guide 
PA
Pennsylvania trucking companies
Pennsylvania is one of the densest Mid-Atlantic freight states. Philadelphia handles Northeast port-driven volume; Pittsburgh anchors the western steel and industrial flatbed market. The state sits on the I-95 / I-80 / I-76 corridor network.See Pennsylvania guide 
IN
Indiana trucking companies
Indiana is the geographic center of the US distribution network — most of the country is reachable within a one-day drive from Indianapolis. Heavy auto-parts JIT freight, FedEx volume, and Amazon fulfillment-driven dry van flow.See Indiana guide 
MI
Michigan trucking companies
Michigan is the heart of the US automotive supply chain. Detroit anchors heavy auto-parts JIT freight, with steady cross-border traffic to and from Canada via the Ambassador Bridge and the Detroit-Windsor Tunnel.See Michigan guide 
MO
Missouri trucking companies
Missouri is the dominant Central US freight state. Kansas City and St Louis together form a balanced east/west freight axis; ag and food-grade volume runs heavy year-round.See Missouri guide 
AZ
Arizona trucking companies
Arizona is the Southwest distribution gateway between LA and the rest of the country. Phoenix anchors year-round reefer staging and dense Texas/Midwest outbound. Equipment shopping is favorable because of dry desert climate preserving used trucks.See Arizona guide 
NY
New York trucking companies
New York — combined with adjacent New Jersey — forms the largest inbound freight market on the East Coast. The Port of NY/NJ is the busiest US container port by some measures. Dense regional flow throughout the Northeast corridor.See New York guide 
WA
Washington trucking companies
Washington is the dominant Pacific Northwest freight state. Seattle / Tacoma forms the third-largest US port complex, with strong outbound containerized freight and a high reefer share from regional agriculture.See Washington guide 
NJ
New Jersey trucking companies
New Jersey is the operational backbone of the New York / NJ port complex — the busiest US container port. Dense inbound containerized freight feeds the Northeast, while the I-78 / I-80 / I-95 corridors carry heavy regional flow.See New Jersey guide 
VA
Virginia trucking companies
Virginia anchors the Mid-Atlantic freight market. The Port of Virginia (Norfolk) is the East Coast's deepest container port and a major auto and military gateway. Inland, the I-81 / I-95 corridors carry dense long-haul flow.See Virginia guide 
WI
Wisconsin trucking companies
Wisconsin is the dairy and paper-products backbone of the Upper Midwest. Milwaukee and Green Bay anchor the freight network, with steady reefer flow from dairy and frozen-food production, plus heavy paper and printing volume.See Wisconsin guide 
OR
Oregon trucking companies
Oregon anchors the Pacific Northwest interior freight network. Portland is the state's freight capital with strong outbound flow to California and Washington. Heavy reefer from the Willamette Valley agricultural belt.See Oregon guide 
KY
Kentucky trucking companies
Kentucky sits at the geographic crossroads of the US distribution network. Louisville hosts the UPS Worldport — the largest air-cargo-to-truck conversion hub in the country — and the state's automotive plants drive heavy JIT freight.See Kentucky guide

Does Numeo replace dispatchers?
No. Across every customer story, dispatchers use Numeo to cut repetitive work, not to remove human judgment. As the Imran IAC dispatch team puts it: "It's making your job easier. It's not taking your job." The dispatcher still evaluates the load, broker, driver fit, and rate before booking.
What size carriers use Numeo?
Everything from one truck to 150+. Published customer stories cover a 5-truck operation, a small-carrier workflow, a 100+ truck operation, and Four Ways Cargo's 150-truck team. These examples are customer-specific; validate time savings and capacity against your own baseline rather than treating any story as a benchmark.
What results have customers actually seen?
Published customer stories describe workflow changes such as less tab switching, faster broker follow-up, and more structured dispatch work. Numeric outcomes are intentionally not presented here until the baseline, measurement period, metric definition, owner, and customer approval are recorded in the claims registry.
Which parts of dispatch do customers use Numeo for?
Across the stories: multi-board load search, broker outreach and rate negotiation, load evaluation, map and route context, booking history, first-pass paperwork checks, scheduling, ETAs, track-and-trace, and automatic broker status updates. Most carriers start with the single biggest time sink and expand from there.
Which customer story should I read first?
Run a larger fleet? Start with Four Ways Cargo or Imran IAC. Run a small fleet? Start with Octopus Express. If your pain is morning chaos, fraud risk, factoring checks, or copy-paste, start with MO Globe Trucking. Each story maps to a workflow you can recognize in your own operation.
Do dispatchers still choose which load to book?
Yes. Numeo surfaces context and advances the repetitive steps, but the dispatcher makes the call on the load, broker, driver fit, schedule, rate, and operational risk. Even in AI Hub's agentic modes, the default keeps a human approval step before anything binding ships.

About Numeo
We build AI agents for trucking carriers.
Numeo helps dispatch teams find better loads, negotiate faster, update brokers, and manage operations with less manual work. Our products work alongside dispatchers across the carrier workflow: load search, broker communication, rate negotiation, document handling, accounting, fleet management, and safety.
Why we exist
Carriers run on too much manual work.
Dispatchers still spend hours every day searching load boards, comparing rates, writing broker emails, updating brokers, checking documents, and moving information between disconnected tools.
That work slows teams down. It limits how many trucks one dispatcher can cover. It makes growth depend on more tabs, more follow-ups, and more manual effort.
Numeo exists to change that.
We believe the future of freight operations is not another dashboard. It is AI agents that can search, reason, communicate, and execute real work alongside dispatchers.
What we do
AI agents for the work behind every load.
Numeo automates the repetitive work that slows dispatch teams down, while keeping dispatchers in control of the decisions that matter.
Our platform helps carriers:
Find and compare loads across connected sources
Identify the best and most profitable matches
Send broker outreach faster
Negotiate rates with AI and market context
Update brokers automatically
Match documents and reduce paperwork
Manage dispatch, accounting, fleet, safety, and operations in one system
The goal is simple: less manual work, faster execution, and more revenue capacity per dispatcher.
Our products
Built for the way dispatch teams actually work.
Numeo Spot
A Chrome extension for DAT that adds one-click emails, factoring checks, auto refresh, filters, route view, toll calculator, profit calculator, click-to-call from the dispatcher screen, copy-load details, templates, broker blacklist, and booking history directly inside the dispatcher workflow.
Load Hub
A centralized load search experience that brings loads from 15+ brokerage load boards into one place, so dispatchers do not have to repeat the same search across every board.
Load Radar
Saved load alerts that notify dispatchers by email, mobile app, or Telegram when a strong match appears across connected sources.
AI Hub
AI search, market rate analysis, and auto negotiation for dispatchers who need to find the right loads and move before someone else books them.
Numeo One TMS
A carrier operations system with accounting, updater assistant, ratecon recognition, fleet management, smart dispatch board, Fuel AI, and safety tools.
Founders
The team building Numeo.
Akmal Paiziev
Co-founder & CEO
Serial founder behind Newmax Technologies, MyTaxi, Workly, Maxtrack, and Express24, which was acquired by Yandex. Akmal has 19+ years of experience building technology for transportation, operations, and high-scale service businesses.
Beka Kodirov
Co-founder & CTO
Engineering leader with experience at Warner Bros. Discovery, Hulu, and fuboTV. Beka previously co-founded Feeba.io and now leads product and engineering at Numeo.
Otabek Yusupov
Co-founder & COO
Operations and finance leader with experience at Deloitte and Amazon, including financial strategy and planning for Amazon's global logistics teams.
How we work
Four principles guide how we build.
Dispatcher-first
Every product starts with a real dispatcher workflow: the clicks, calls, checks, follow-ups, and decisions that happen every day.
Automate the manual work
AI should handle the repetitive work: searching, checking, drafting, updating, matching, and filing. Dispatchers should spend more time on judgment, relationships, and revenue decisions.
Ship fast, learn faster
We build quickly, test with real users, and improve based on what actually helps dispatch teams move faster.
Carriers deserve better tools
Brokers have invested heavily in technology. Carriers are still stuck with too many spreadsheets, phone calls, tabs, and disconnected systems. Numeo closes that gap.
FAQ
Frequently asked questionsStill have questions? Book a demo→See all frequently asked questions →
What is Numeo?
Numeo is an AI dispatch platform for US trucking carriers. Its products — the Numeo Spot Chrome extension, Load Hub multi-board search, AI Hub agent, the Numeo App, and the Numeo One AI-native TMS — help dispatch teams find loads, negotiate rates, update brokers, and run back-office operations with less manual work.
Why did Numeo focus on trucking carriers?
Brokers have invested heavily in technology while carriers were left on spreadsheets, phones, and dozens of browser tabs. A dispatcher's day runs 10–12 hours, but only 1–2 are the booking work that actually pays. Numeo's mission is to close that gap with AI agents that search, negotiate, communicate, and execute alongside dispatchers — not another dashboard.
Who is behind Numeo?
Numeo AI is based in Palo Alto, CA, and led by founders Akmal Paiziev (CEO; previously built Express24, acquired by Yandex), Beka Kodirov (CTO; engineering leadership at Warner Bros. Discovery, Hulu, fuboTV), and Otabek Yusupov (COO; previously Deloitte and Amazon logistics finance).
How is Numeo different from a generic AI tool or a traditional TMS?
Numeo is built specifically around carrier dispatch workflows — load search across boards, AI rate negotiation by email, automatic broker updates, and an AI-native TMS — rather than a general chatbot or a record-keeping-first legacy system. It layers onto the tools you already use instead of forcing a rip-and-replace.
Does Numeo fit both small and large carriers?
Yes, with different entry points. Owner-operators and solo dispatchers start with the free Numeo App or Spot; small fleets add Spot Ultra and Numeo One; mid-size and larger fleets run Numeo One with AI Hub for dispatch capacity, accounting, and compliance in one platform.

Trust & Security
How Numeo secures your data across Numeo Spot, Numeo One, and our AI services — managed databases on Google Cloud, encryption everywhere, layered access controls, and clear limits on how your data is used.
Quick answer
How does Numeo protect customer data?
Numeo describes a layered security model built on Google Cloud, encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege access, managed databases, and OAuth connections for Gmail and Outlook. The page also explains what email data Numeo accesses and why; customers should verify the current report and contract terms for their own compliance review.

Enterprise Security

01
Our security approach
Numeo powers dispatch, communications, accounting, and fleet operations for carriers, brokers, and dispatchers who work with sensitive operational and financial data every day. Security is built into how we design, build, and run the platform — across Numeo Spot, Numeo One, and our AI services.
At a high level, we focus on:
Enterprise-grade cloud infrastructure on Google Cloud.
Encryption of data in transit and at rest.
Layered network and access controls, with least-privilege access and continuous monitoring.
Clear limits on what data we use and why.
02
Infrastructure and hosting
Numeo runs on Google Cloud, using managed, security-hardened infrastructure so we can focus on protecting your data rather than patching servers.
Hosted on Google Cloud, with managed patching and infrastructure maintained by Google.
Customer data encrypted at rest with AES-256.
All connections encrypted in transit.
Continuous security monitoring, logging, and alerting across production.
03
How and where we store your data
Everything you see in Numeo — your account, your loads, your drivers, your emails — lives in managed, security-hardened databases on Google Cloud.
Email content (the messages Numeo reads to power features like rate-confirmation capture and AI replies) is stored in a managed PostgreSQL database on Google Cloud.
Account and operational data (users, companies, loads, drivers, brokers) is stored in MongoDB Atlas, MongoDB’s managed and independently audited cloud service.
Payment card data never touches our servers. All payments are processed by Stripe, a PCI-DSS Level 1 certified provider. We store only your subscription status — never card numbers.
Both databases encrypt all data at rest with AES-256, and every connection to them — including from our own services — is encrypted in transit.
04
Why your data is safe: layers, not a single lock
No single safeguard protects your data — several independent layers do, and an attacker would need to defeat all of them at once:
Layer 1 — Our databases are not reachable from the internet.
They only accept connections from approved network locations: our production services and a small, fixed set of approved addresses. If anyone else tries to connect — even with a valid username and password — the connection is refused before a password is ever checked.
Layer 2 — Credentials live in a vault, not in code.
Database passwords and connection details are never written into our source code. They are kept in Google Secret Manager, Google Cloud’s encrypted secrets vault, and delivered to our services only at deployment. Even if our entire source code leaked, it would contain no way in — and even if a credential somehow leaked, Layer 1 still blocks the connection from any unapproved location.
Layer 3 — Access is least-privilege and personal.
Production access is granted per person, by an administrator, with the minimum permissions needed. Nobody at Numeo has standing access to customer data “just in case,” and access is logged and monitored.
Layer 4 — Your password can't be read, even by us.
We never store your password. We store only a salted one-way cryptographic hash, which cannot be reversed back into your password — not by an attacker, and not by us.
05
How Numeo connects to your email
When you connect Gmail or Outlook, Numeo uses the provider’s standard OAuth flow:
You log in on Google or Microsoft, not inside Numeo.
Google or Microsoft ask you to approve the requested permissions.
If you agree, they issue secure tokens that let Numeo send and read email only in the scopes you approved — without sharing your password.
We never see or store your email password. Access tokens are stored securely and can be revoked at any time — disconnect from your provider or your Numeo settings and we revoke our access.
06
What data we access (and why)
To power features like 1-Click Emails, AI Emails, rate-confirmation capture, follow-ups, and booking history, Numeo needs limited access to your email:
Send emails to brokers from your connected account, at your direction.
Read emails related to loads and brokers so we can:
Extract load and rate-confirmation details.
Match replies to loads.
Build your recent booking history.
Under Google’s Limited Use requirements, which we commit to in our Privacy Policy, your email data may not be used for advertising, sold, read by humans outside narrow consented cases, or used to train AI models.
07
SOC 2 and compliance
Numeo maintains SOC 2 Type II certification. Our SOC 2 Type II audit independently verifies that the controls described on this page — access management, monitoring, encryption, and secure development — exist and operate.
Our program emphasizes:
Access control and least-privilege access.
Monitoring and logging of system activity.
Secure development and change management.
Our cloud provider and other subprocessors are also independently audited against SOC 2 Type II and similar frameworks; our email infrastructure provider is ISO 27001 certified. Customers and their compliance teams can request our SOC 2 Type II report under NDA — contact support@numeo.ai.
08
Subprocessors and AI providers
Numeo works with a limited set of vetted subprocessors to deliver the platform:
Cloud hosting and databases (Google Cloud, MongoDB Atlas) and payments (Stripe).
Email and calendar connectivity for the providers you connect (Google, Microsoft).
Enterprise AI providers — Microsoft Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Google (Vertex AI / Gemini), and Anthropic.
AI providers process your data only to deliver the features you request, under enterprise terms that prohibit using it to train their models. We do not sell your data or use it for advertising. A current list of subprocessors is available on request, and our Privacy Policy details how Google user data is handled under Google’s Limited Use requirements.
09
If you have security questions
If you have any questions about security, data protection, or compliance:
Contact us at support@numeo.ai.
Or reach out through the in-app support widget.
We’re happy to coordinate with your IT or compliance team.

Frequently asked questionsStill have questions? Book a demo→See all frequently asked questions →
How does Numeo protect my data and connected accounts?
Your data lives in managed databases on Google Cloud — PostgreSQL for email content, MongoDB Atlas for account and operational data — encrypted at rest with AES-256 and reachable only from approved network locations. Numeo maintains SOC 2 Type II certification; our email infrastructure provider is additionally ISO 27001 certified. Email connects via OAuth 2.0 for Gmail and Outlook, so Numeo never sees or stores your email password; access tokens are stored securely and revocable anytime, and access follows least-privilege controls with monitoring and logging.
How exactly is our data saved — and who can read it?
Your data is stored in managed databases on Google Cloud — PostgreSQL for email content, MongoDB Atlas for account and operational data — encrypted at rest with AES-256. Those databases are not reachable from the public internet: they accept connections only from our production systems and a fixed set of approved addresses. Inside Numeo, access is granted per person, with least-privilege permissions, and is logged. In practice, the only thing reading your data day-to-day is the product itself, doing what you asked it to do.
You say it's safe — what actually stops a hacker?
Several independent layers, each of which must fail before any data is exposed. A stolen database password alone gets an attacker nothing, because our databases refuse connections from unapproved network locations. Stealing our source code gets them nothing, because credentials aren't in the code — they live in Google Secret Manager, an encrypted vault. Even someone holding a full connection string would still be stopped at the network layer. On top of that, the data itself is encrypted at rest, every connection is encrypted in transit, and your login password exists only as an irreversible salted hash.
Can you prove it — for example, with our emails?
Yes — follow the life of one email. When a broker replies to you, Numeo receives it over an encrypted connection using the scoped permission you granted when you connected your inbox (we never see or store your email password). The message is stored in a database that is encrypted at rest and unreachable from the public internet. Under Google's Limited Use requirements, which we commit to in our Privacy Policy, that email may not be used for advertising, sold, read by humans outside narrow consented cases, or used to train AI models. And our SOC 2 Type II audit independently verifies these controls exist and operate — customers can request the report under NDA at support@numeo.ai.
What email data does Numeo access, and how is it used?
Scope is deliberately limited: Numeo sends broker emails from your connected account and reads load- and broker-related emails to power booking history and reply matching. That data is never used for advertising, never resold, and never shared with third parties. You can disconnect and revoke access at any time.
Is Numeo SOC 2 Type II certified?
Yes — Numeo maintains SOC 2 Type II certification, and our email infrastructure provider is additionally ISO 27001 certified. Our SOC 2 Type II audit independently verifies our security controls; qualified buyers can request the report under NDA at support@numeo.ai.
What should our IT or operations team ask before adopting Numeo?
Good questions to cover: how credentials are handled (OAuth, no stored passwords), what email scope is granted, how access is logged and revoked, what data is retained, and which compliance attestations apply (Numeo holds SOC 2 Type II; our email infrastructure provider is ISO 27001 certified). Numeo's security team can walk through each.
Who should review Numeo's security before rollout?
Operations leaders, IT/security, and compliance staff — anyone responsible for systems that touch dispatch, broker communication, documents, or customer commitments. Because Numeo connects to email and load boards, a quick security review up front keeps adoption smooth.

Hotshot Trucking: Pay, Costs & How to Start
A straight guide to hotshot trucking — the CDL threshold, real startup costs, what the freight pays, and the honest case for and against running it as a business.
Guide
Hotshot Trucking: Pay, Costs & How to Start26,001 lbs
numeo
What hotshot trucking actually is
Hotshot trucking is hauling smaller, time-sensitive loads on a medium-duty pickup pulling a gooseneck or flatbed trailer, rather than on a Class 8 tractor. The trucks are usually one-ton duallies — a Ram 3500, an F-350 or F-450, a Silverado 3500 — and the trailers are typically 30 to 40 feet.
The name comes from the freight, not the truck. A hotshot load is one somebody needs now: a replacement part for a drilling rig that is losing money every hour it sits, a piece of equipment a construction crew cannot work without, a pallet that missed its LTL cutoff. Urgency is the product. That is why the rates hold up on lanes where a 53-foot dry van would not bother.
The freight skews toward oil and gas, construction, agriculture and machinery, and it concentrates in Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, North Dakota and the industrial Southeast.
Do you need a CDL for hotshot?
This is the question that brings most people to the topic, and the answer turns on one number: 26,001 pounds.
If the gross combination weight rating of your truck and trailer together is 26,001 lbs or more, and the trailer is rated over 10,000 lbs, you need a Class A CDL. Below that, you generally do not.
This is why so much hotshot runs on a one-ton dually pulling a 40-foot gooseneck: it is the largest practical setup that can be kept under the line. A truck rated at 14,000 lbs GVWR with a trailer rated at 11,999 lbs comes to 25,999 — deliberately.
Two things people get wrong about this:
It is ratings, not actual weight. The thresholds use GVWR and GCWR — the manufacturer's ratings on the door sticker and the trailer plate. Running an empty trailer does not put you under the line if the ratings say otherwise.
No CDL does not mean no regulation. If you are operating in interstate commerce with a vehicle over 10,000 lbs GVWR or GCWR, you are a commercial motor vehicle operator. You need a USDOT number, and for for-hire work, MC operating authority. The federal safety regulations apply to you: hours of service, medical certification, vehicle inspections, the lot. The CDL threshold and the regulatory threshold are two different lines, and the regulatory one sits far lower.
If you are unclear whether your freight is even interstate, that question is worth settling first — our guide to interstate vs intrastate trucking covers the loads that cross the line without leaving the state.
What it costs to start
Hotshot's real appeal is the entry price. A Class 8 tractor and a 53-foot trailer is a serious capital commitment; a used dually and a gooseneck is not.
Rough ranges, and they move with the used-truck market:
Truck. A used one-ton dually in workable condition typically runs $25,000–$55,000. New is $70,000+.
Trailer. A 40-foot gooseneck runs roughly $10,000–$25,000 depending on deck type and condition.
Authority and registration. MC authority and USDOT registration, plus the BOC-3 filing and UCR. Several hundred dollars, plus a filing service if you use one.
Insurance. The line item that surprises people. Expect $8,000–$16,000 a year for a new authority, and higher in the first year because you have no loss history. Brokers will generally want $1,000,000 in liability and $100,000 in cargo before they tender you anything, regardless of the lower federal minimum.
Working capital. Brokers pay on 30-day terms as standard. You need enough cash — or a factoring arrangement — to cover fuel and payments for the six-plus weeks before the first invoices land.
All in, a realistic startup number is $45,000–$90,000 including a genuine reserve. The people who fail at this almost never fail because they bought the wrong truck. They fail because they budgeted for the truck and not for the ten weeks before the money starts arriving.
What hotshot pays
Hotshot rates are usually quoted per mile and are higher than dry van on comparable lanes — the premium is for urgency and for the fact that fewer trucks can take the load on short notice.
The number that actually matters is not the rate. It is the rate minus what the mile costs you. ATRI put the marginal cost of trucking at roughly $2.26 per mile in 2024, and while a hotshot rig runs cheaper than a Class 8 on fuel and tyres, it is not dramatically cheaper once you include insurance, maintenance and the depreciation of a truck being worked far harder than it was designed for.
Two structural facts about hotshot economics that the rate-per-mile conversation hides:
Deadhead hurts more. Hotshot loads are small and often one-directional — into an oilfield, onto a job site. There is frequently nothing to bring back. A $3.00/mile load that requires a 200-mile empty return is not a $3.00/mile load.
Capacity is your ceiling. A hotshot trailer takes a fraction of what a 53-foot van does. You cannot solve a bad rate with volume the way a Class 8 operator can.
The operators who make hotshot work treat reloads as the whole game. The ones who struggle chase headline rates and drive home empty.
Hotshot vs a Class 8 truck
HotshotClass 8Entry cost$45,000–$90,000$150,000+CDLOften not requiredClass A requiredCapacity~16,000–20,000 lbs~45,000 lbsRate per mileHigherLowerRevenue per loadLowerHigherDeadhead riskHigherLowerMaintenanceConsumer-grade parts, shorter service life under loadPurpose-built, longer intervals
The honest summary: hotshot is the cheaper way in and the harder way to scale. It is a strong fit for someone entering the industry with limited capital, in a region with real hotshot demand, who is prepared to hustle reloads. It is a poor fit for someone who wants predictable weekly revenue with less operational attention.
The freight niches worth knowing
Hotshot is not one market. The operators who do well usually pick a niche and get known in it, because repeat shippers beat board freight on both rate and deadhead.
Oil and gas. The origin of hotshot and still its centre of gravity. Rig parts, valves, pumps, tubing — freight where a delay costs the customer far more than the haul does, which is why it pays. Concentrated in the Permian, the Bakken, the Eagle Ford and Oklahoma. Highly cyclical: it follows the rig count, and when drilling slows the freight disappears fast.
Construction and equipment. Skid steers, mini excavators, scaffolding, materials to a job site with a crew standing around waiting. Steadier than oilfield and less weather-dependent, though it competes more directly with flatbed.
Agriculture. Implements, parts, hay, livestock equipment. Strongly seasonal, and relationships matter more than boards — a lot of this freight never gets posted.
Auto and machinery transport. Vehicles, tractors, small industrial machines. Requires the right deck and tie-down setup, and often specific cargo coverage.
The pattern across all four is the same: the profitable work comes from shippers who call you directly. Boards are how you fill the gaps and how you get started, not where a mature hotshot operation gets most of its freight.
Finding hotshot loads
Hotshot is a filtering problem more than a searching problem. Most general load boards treat it as a subcategory of flatbed, if they categorise it at all, and a posting that suits a 48-foot step deck will not suit a 40-foot gooseneck. Time spent opening loads you cannot legally or physically take is the single largest waste in a hotshot operator's day.
What separates a workable board from a frustrating one:
Filtering by equipment and length, not just "flatbed"
Weight filters that respect your actual capacity, so you are not reading loads that would put you over
Deadhead radius on the search, because the return leg decides whether the load pays
Alerts, because hotshot freight is urgent by definition and the good loads are covered in minutes, not hours
Several free boards will do this. We compare what each one's free tier actually includes — including the ones that cap your searches or charge for the tools that make the board useful — in our guide to free load boards.
Where dispatch fits
The hard part of hotshot is not driving. It is that the same person is driving and dispatching, and those two jobs want the same hours.
You cannot search boards while you are under a load, which means the reload gets worked out at a truck stop after a ten-hour day, when the good freight has already gone. The operators who run hotshot profitably are the ones who have solved that timing problem — either by paying a dispatcher a percentage of gross, or by automating the search so that matching loads surface without someone sitting in front of a board.
That is the specific gap we build for. Numeo watches every connected board at once, ranks what appears against your actual costs, deadhead and equipment rather than by posting time, and pushes alerts when something fits — so the reload is lined up before the trailer is empty, not after. For an operator whose profitability lives or dies on the return leg, that is not a convenience feature.
See how it works in Numeo Spot inside the boards you already use, or in Numeo One once the load is booked and there is an invoice to chase. Both start free.
Figures in this guide are typical market ranges, not quotes, and regulatory thresholds should be verified with FMCSA and your state before you buy anything.

Interstate vs Intrastate Trucking: The Complete Guide
The legal difference between interstate and intrastate trucking, the loads that cross the line without leaving the state, and what changes for authority, HOS, driver age and insurance.
Guide
Interstate vs Intrastate Trucking: The Complete Guide49 CFR 390.5
numeo
The difference in one sentence
Intrastate trucking stays inside one state. Interstate trucking crosses a state line — or carries freight that does.
That second half is where carriers get caught. A truck that never leaves Texas can still be operating in interstate commerce, subject to federal rules, with a driver who has to be 21 and an authority that has to come from Washington rather than Austin. The state line the truck crosses is not the only line that matters. The one the freight crosses matters more.
What the regulation actually says
The definitions live in 49 CFR 390.5. Interstate commerce means trade, traffic, or transportation:
between a place in a State and a place outside of such State (including a place outside of the United States);
between two places in a State through another State or a place outside of the United States; or
between two places in a State as part of trade, traffic, or transportation originating or terminating outside the State or the United States.
Intrastate commerce is defined by exclusion: any trade, traffic, or transportation in any State which is not described in the term "interstate commerce."
Read that third bullet again, because it is the one that decides most arguments. It says nothing about where the truck goes. It asks where the freight started and where it is ultimately going.
The trap: intrastate moves that are legally interstate
Three examples of trucks that never leave the state and are in interstate commerce anyway:
The drayage run. A container lands at the Port of Los Angeles and you haul it to a warehouse in Fontana. Ninety miles, one state. But the goods originated in Asia, so the move is part of a continuous journey that began outside the United States. Interstate.
The Laredo pull. Freight crosses from Mexico, and you take it from a Laredo yard to a distribution centre in Dallas. Both ends are in Texas. The freight's journey is not.
The final leg. A shipper in Georgia sends goods to a cross-dock in Atlanta, and you run the last 60 miles to Savannah. If that cross-dock is a waypoint rather than a genuine destination — if the goods were always headed to Savannah — the whole movement is one interstate journey and your leg is part of it.
The legal test is the continuity of the freight's journey, not the length of your leg. A stop at a warehouse does not break the chain if the goods were always intended to keep moving. That intent is usually established by the bill of lading and by whether the shipper had a fixed destination in mind before the goods started moving.
The practical version, for a dispatcher deciding whether to accept a load: if the freight came from out of state or is going out of state, treat it as interstate, regardless of what your truck's odometer says.
What changes when you are in interstate commerce
1. Operating authority
Both interstate and intrastate carriers need a USDOT number — that surprises people who assume it is a federal-only requirement. It is the identifier FMCSA uses to track a company's safety record, and most states now require it for intrastate operation too.
What is different is operating authority. A for-hire interstate carrier hauling regulated commodities needs MC authority from FMCSA on top of the USDOT number. A purely intrastate for-hire carrier deals with its own state's regulator instead, and the requirements vary enormously — some states are close to federal, others are far lighter.
2. Driver age
This is the most consequential practical difference for a small fleet trying to hire. To drive a CMV in interstate commerce, a driver must be 21. In most states, an 18-year-old with a CDL can drive intrastate.
That gap is why plenty of young drivers spend two or three years running in-state work before they can take a load across a line. It is also why a carrier that drifts into interstate freight without noticing can find itself with a driver who was legal on Friday and is not on Monday.
3. Hours of service
Federal HOS rules for property-carrying drivers are the ones most people can recite: 11 hours of driving within a 14-hour on-duty window, after 10 consecutive hours off, with a 60-hour/7-day or 70-hour/8-day limit.
Intrastate HOS is set by the state. Most states have adopted the federal rules for intrastate carriers with modifications, and the modifications are usually more generous — a longer driving limit or a longer window. Texas, for example, runs a longer intrastate window than the federal standard. California has its own intrastate variations.
Do not take a number from a blog post — including this one — as the rule for your state. Check with your state's DOT or public utility commission, because the differences are real, they change, and the penalty for getting it wrong falls on you.
4. Medical certification
Interstate drivers need a current medical examiner's certificate from a provider on FMCSA's National Registry, and the certificate has to stay current and linked to the CDL.
Intrastate medical standards are set by the state, and several states run waiver programmes for conditions that would disqualify a driver federally — which is exactly why some drivers are intrastate-only by choice rather than by preference.
5. Insurance minimums
The federal financial-responsibility minimum for general freight in interstate commerce is $750,000 of liability coverage. In practice almost nobody runs at that level, because brokers and shippers routinely require $1,000,000 before they will tender a load, and many require more for specific commodities.
Intrastate minimums are set by the state and are often lower. That lower floor is not much use if the brokers you want to work with all require $1M anyway — which is why carriers planning to grow generally buy to the market's requirement, not the regulation's.
6. Drug and alcohol testing
Testing under 49 CFR Part 382 applies to CDL drivers, and it reaches intrastate CDL drivers too — this is not a federal-only obligation. If you hold a CDL and operate a CMV, you are in a testing programme and in the Clearinghouse. Carriers that assume intrastate means exempt tend to find out during an audit.
Which one should you run?
Intrastate is the smaller regulatory surface: no MC authority, lower insurance floor in many states, and you can hire at 18 in most places. If your freight genuinely originates and terminates in-state — construction aggregate, local distribution, in-state agriculture — there is no reason to take on federal obligations you do not need.
Interstate is the bigger market, and it is not close. The long-haul lanes, the national brokers, the reload options that keep a truck from running empty — those are interstate. A carrier confined to one state is competing for a fraction of the available freight and has far fewer options when its home market softens.
The honest answer for most for-hire carriers is that interstate authority is worth the overhead, and the ones who regret it are usually the ones who got there by accident: they took a load that turned out to be interstate, without the authority, the insurance limits, or a 21-year-old driver.
How this varies across the U.S.
Intrastate rules are genuinely state-by-state, and the states with the most freight tend to have the most specific requirements. Texas, California, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Ohio, Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Tennessee and Arizona each run their own intrastate authority and HOS regimes, and the differences between neighbours can be substantial.
The states with major international gateways deserve extra care, because the third bullet of 390.5 does the most work there. Texas border crossings at Laredo and El Paso, the Southern California ports, and the Gulf ports all generate large volumes of short in-state moves that are legally interstate from the first mile.
Where dispatch fits
The classification problem is a dispatch problem before it is a compliance problem, because the decision gets made when someone accepts a load — not when the auditor arrives.
That decision is usually made fast, off a board posting that says where the load picks up and delivers and nothing about where the freight has been. A dispatcher covering several trucks has minutes per load, and "is this secretly interstate?" is not a question a posting answers on its own. The signals are there — a pickup at a port or a border yard, a shipper who is a freight forwarder rather than a manufacturer, a BOL that references an earlier leg — but somebody has to notice them.
The other half is commercial. Interstate authority is only worth its overhead if the trucks actually run the interstate freight that justifies it, and that comes down to whether your dispatcher can see enough of the market to keep the trucks loaded on the lanes that pay. That is the part we build for: Numeo ranks loads against your real costs and lanes rather than by posting time, and searches every connected board at once so the reload options are visible before the truck is empty rather than after.
If you are weighing the move to interstate, the arithmetic is simpler than the regulation: the authority, the insurance and the 21-year-old driver are fixed costs, and they are paid for by the freight you can only reach with them. See how the load side works in Numeo Spot and Numeo One, or compare what the free load boards show you before you pay for anything.
This guide is general information, not legal advice. Verify your obligations with FMCSA and your state regulator before you change how you operate.
