Add your MC and company
Enter your MC number and let FMCSA autofill your company details. Run up to 5 companies from one account.
3 min read

Setting up your company in Numeo One starts with your MC number. Type it in and FMCSA fills in the rest — company name, address, and authority details — so you don't have to key it all by hand. Running more than one authority? You can add up to 5 companies from the same account.

Add your MC number

On the onboarding screen, enter your 6-digit MC number (the field shows 000000 as a placeholder).

As you type, Numeo searches FMCSA in the background:


If FMCSA finds a match, pick it from the suggestions dropdown and your company details autofill.

If FMCSA returns nothing, you can type every field in manually — nothing is blocked.



Animated demo
Entering your MC number with FMCSA suggestions
A short screen recording will be added here.

Verify your MC

You can confirm your MC any time from Settings → General, in the MC verification section. Verifying your authority keeps your company details accurate on invoices, tracking links, and broker-facing messages.

Run more than one MC

If you dispatch under more than one authority, you can add each as its own company:


Add a company for each MC you run.

Each MC has to be unique — Numeo won't let you add the same MC twice on one account.

You can hold up to 5 companies on a single account.


Across the ongoing-loads board and other tables, you can filter by company or MC so you're only looking at the loads for one authority at a time.


A single combined view across all your companies for multi-MC stakeholders is coming soon. For now, filter by company where you need to.

Payroll, fuel & IFTAIntermediate
Fuel tracking and reconciliation
Track fuel against the truck's GPS trail, reconcile fuel-card transactions like WEX, and catch out-of-route or over-priced stops.
4 min read

Numeo One brings your fuel spend into the same workspace as your loads and pay. It reconciles fuel-card transactions against where the truck actually was, so a stop that's out of route or over-priced stands out instead of slipping through. Fuel lives under Accounting, alongside pay and invoicing.

Reconcile your fuel card

Connect your fuel-card provider and Numeo matches each transaction to the truck and load it belongs to:


Fuel-card data reconciles against your transactions — for example, WEX.

Each purchase is tied back to the truck, so you can see fuel by truck and by load, not just a stack of receipts.


You do the checking, not the data entry.

Fuel against the GPS trail

Numeo checks fuel purchases against the truck's GPS trail — the same live location feed your ELD provides. Two things get easier:


Out-of-route stops — a fill-up far off the planned lane is easy to spot when the purchase sits next to where the truck actually drove.

Expensive-zone stops — fuel bought in a pricey area, when a cheaper stop was close, gets flagged against your dispatch rules.


Numeo's fuel checks can also read your dispatch messages and expensive-zone rules, so the flags line up with how you already dispatch.

Fuel flows into pay and accounting

Reconciled fuel isn't a dead end — it feeds the rest of your back office:


Fuel costs roll into driver and contractor pay as part of each statement's cost breakdown. See Driver and contractor pay.

Fuel is one of the two numbers IFTA needs. See IFTA mileage and fuel reports.


Good to know


Fuel reconciliation leans on live truck location, so a connected ELD makes the GPS-trail checks work. See Connect your ELD.

Fuel-card and toll providers connect from Settings — see the integrations directory.

Fuel depth can vary by plan — check the pricing page.

Driver communicationBeginner
Driver notifications over Telegram
Set up automatic driver alerts — arrival and departure, wakeup calls, idle, ELD offline, detention, and heavy load.
4 min read

Numeo One sends your drivers automatic status alerts over Telegram — so you're not calling every truck for an ETA. Turn on the alerts you want per load, and the system watches the truck and messages the driver when something changes.


Screenshot
A load's notification settings with alert toggles
A product screenshot will be added here.

Before you start

The location-based alerts (arrival, departure, idle, ELD offline) need a connected ELD — that's where live truck location and Hours of Service come from. Connect one first: see Connect your ELD. Alerts that don't depend on location, like the wakeup call or heavy load, work off the load's schedule and paperwork.

Where notifications live

Notification settings sit on each load. Open a load on the Ongoing Loads board and open its notification settings. Each alert is a checkbox with its own threshold — minutes, hours, or a weight. Turn on the ones that matter for that load. You can also set defaults so new loads start with your usual alerts already on.

The alerts you can turn on

Arrival and departure (needs ELD):


Nearby Stop Detection — fires the moment the truck first enters the stop's geofence.

Arrival Detection — fires once the truck has stayed inside the stop geofence for about 10 minutes, so a drive-by doesn't trigger it.

Departure Detection — fires after the truck leaves the stop geofence.


Keeping drivers moving:


Driver Wakeup Call — a reminder to the driver before a planned departure.

Idle Time — when a truck sits stopped longer than your idle threshold (in minutes).

Delays — when a load is running later than your delay threshold.


Equipment and load:


ELD Offline Alert — messages the driver when their ELD stops reporting location. This one always goes to the driver only.

Heavy Load Alert — when the BOL's total weight is over your threshold (default 42,000 lbs).


Getting paid for waiting:


Detention Alert — a final notice with the total detention time when the truck departs after sitting in detention.


Good to know


Every alert has its own threshold — set the minutes, hours, or weight that fit your operation.

Send Update controls how often automatic status updates go out while a truck is in transit, in "Automated Updates" or "Semi-Automated Updates" mode.

There are more alerts than the common ones above — Long Loading, Long Unloading, Speed Alert, Missing Paperwork (BOL or POD missing), and Safety Events (harsh braking, hard acceleration, crashes). Turn on what you need per load.

Who each alert goes to — driver, dispatcher, broker, or a custom group — is a separate setting. See Notification recipients and templates.

Dispatch & schedulingIntermediate
Using the scheduler and dispatch board
Drag and drop to assign trucks and drivers, with overlap suggestions and driver-status checks that keep bad assignments off the board.
4 min read

The scheduler is where you match trucks and drivers to loads. Drag a truck onto a load and it's assigned — Numeo checks for conflicts as you go and flags any that overlap, so you're not double-booking a truck by accident.


Screenshot
The scheduler with trucks and drivers
A product screenshot will be added here.

Assign by drag and drop

Assigning is a drag: pick up a truck and drop it onto the load you want it on. Numeo books the assignment and pushes it out — the driver gets a load-assigned notification with the details.

If the truck you're assigning is already committed to another load in that window, Numeo surfaces the overlap and asks you to confirm before it books over it. Nothing gets double-booked silently.

Pair drivers with trucks

Each truck carries its drivers with it. From the "Set Up Your Fleet" quick-assign step, you pair drivers to trucks:


Assign drivers to trucks. Each truck supports up to 2 drivers.


Two drivers per truck covers team operations. Once a truck's drivers are set, assigning the truck to a load assigns the right driver along with it.


Animated demo
Quick-assigning drivers to trucks
A short screen recording will be added here.

Overlap and availability suggestions

When several loads need trucks, Numeo does the first pass for you:


Smart suggestions recommend which truck fits which load, so you're reacting to a shortlist instead of a blank board.

Overlap suggestions can be applied in a batch when you're clearing a stack of loads at once.


You stay in control — the suggestions are a starting point, and you make the final call on every assignment.

Driver status keeps bad assignments out

Every driver is active, inactive, or terminated. Numeo uses that status to protect the board:


Active drivers assign normally.

Inactive or terminated drivers are blocked from assignment — and that block can't be overridden. A driver who's off the road can't accidentally end up on a load.


When a driver leaves, setting their status (including a termination date) keeps them out of future assignments automatically.

The dispatch board

Assigned loads flow onto your live dispatch board, where you watch them run and track them to delivery. See The ongoing loads board for filters, columns, and load statuses — and Live tracking, ETA, and geofences for how each load tracks itself once it's rolling.

Good to know


Drivers pull in automatically when you connect your ELD — Numeo can auto-assign them to trucks from the ELD's vehicle data, so you're editing a mostly-built fleet instead of starting from scratch.

Driver communicationIntermediate
Safety, speed, and equipment alerts
Set up Safety Events, Speed, Heavy Load, ELD Offline, Missing Paperwork, and Delay alerts — plus how Send Update modes work.
4 min read

Beyond arrival and departure, Numeo One can warn you about hard driving, speeding, an overweight BOL, an ELD that's gone quiet, missing paperwork, and a load running late. Turn on the ones that matter per load and route them to the right people.

Turning alerts on and picking recipients is covered in Driver notifications over Telegram and Notification recipients and templates. The ELD-based alerts here need a connected ELD.

Safety and speed


Safety Events — high-severity events from the ELD: harsh braking, hard acceleration, and crashes. No threshold to set.

Speed Alert — fires when a truck's speed goes over your threshold (in mph).


Equipment and load


ELD Offline Alert — messages the driver when their ELD stops reporting location for longer than your threshold (in minutes). This one always goes to the driver only — it's the fastest way to get location flowing again.

Heavy Load Alert — fires when the BOL's total weight is over your threshold. The default is 42,000 lbs. Use it to catch an overweight load before the truck rolls.


Paperwork and delays


Missing Paperwork — fires when a required document like the BOL or POD is missing from a load. No threshold.

Delays — fires when a load is running later than your delay threshold (in minutes).


Send Update modes

Send Update controls how often automatic status updates go out while a truck is in transit — you set the cadence in hours. It runs in one of two modes:


Automated Updates — Numeo sends the update on schedule on its own.

Semi-Automated Updates — you review before each update goes out, so you stay in control of what the broker sees.


An Exclude Delay toggle lets you keep delay notices out of these routine updates when you'd rather send those separately.

Good to know


Every threshold is per load, so an over-dimensional run and a light LTL can have different limits.

Heavy Load Alert reads the weight off the load's BOL — see Bills of lading and load paperwork for where that data comes from.

Location and dwell alerts (arrival, departure, idle, detention) are on their own page — see Arrival, departure, and dwell alerts.

Dispatch & schedulingIntermediate
Driver and truck profiles
Add and import drivers, pair up to 2 drivers per truck, read the CDL automatically, and keep each driver's status current.
4 min read

Trucks and drivers each have a profile in Numeo One. This is where you add drivers, pair them to trucks, and keep each driver's status current — so the scheduler always has the right people to work with.


Screenshot
A truck profile with its assigned drivers
A product screenshot will be added here.

Trucks and their drivers

Each truck carries its drivers with it. From a truck's profile you assign drivers to it — up to 2 drivers per truck, which covers team operations. Once a truck's drivers are set, assigning that truck to a load brings the right driver along automatically.

You can assign drivers from the truck profile or from the "Set Up Your Fleet" quick-assign step on the scheduler — see Using the scheduler and dispatch board.

Add drivers

You don't have to key drivers in one at a time:


Import drivers — bring your roster in as a batch instead of typing each one.

Auto-assign from your ELD — when your ELD is connected, Numeo can pull drivers from the vehicle data and pair them to trucks for you. See Connect your ELD.

CDL parsing — when you add a driver, Numeo can read the CDL and fill in the details for you, so you're checking a pre-filled form instead of typing everything.


Driver status

Every driver is active, inactive, or terminated. You mark the status right on the driver, and set a Driver Termination Date when someone leaves.

Status isn't just a label — it controls whether a driver can be assigned. Inactive and terminated drivers are blocked from assignment and can't be overridden. See Assignment overlaps and driver availability for how that plays out on the board.

Driver notifications

When you assign or change a load, the driver hears about it. Numeo sends a load-assigned, load-unassigned, or load-update notification so the driver always has the current version of the job.

Good to know


Because ELD auto-assign builds most of your fleet for you, adding drivers is usually about filling gaps and keeping statuses current, not starting from scratch.

Troubleshooting & FAQPower user
A rate confirmation didn't create a load
Why a RateCon didn't become a load — a duplicate lock on the same file, a "not a rate confirmation" result, or a non-RC PDF — and how to fix it.
4 min read

You forwarded a rate confirmation and no load showed up. Almost always it's one of three things: the same file was already handled, the attachment wasn't recognized as a rate confirmation, or it wasn't a rate confirmation at all. Here's how to tell which — and what to do.

First, check the board

Before anything else, look at your Ongoing Loads board for the load under the source Rate Confirmation. The most common reason a "missing" load isn't missing is that it already came through. If it's there, you're done.

It's a duplicate of one already handled

Numeo fingerprints each rate confirmation and skips duplicates so you don't get two copies of the same load. If the exact same rate confirmation file comes in again within a 24-hour window, Numeo treats it as the one it already handled and doesn't create a second load.

What to do:


If the load is already on the board, no action needed — this is the system working.

If the load's details changed, update the existing load instead of resending the same file.

If you genuinely need the file re-read, wait out the 24-hour window or reach out to support so it doesn't collide with the earlier copy.


See Rate confirmation email extraction for how duplicate protection works.

It wasn't recognized as a rate confirmation

Numeo reads the attachment and decides whether it's a rate confirmation. If it comes back as "not a rate confirmation," no load is created — that's the guard that keeps random PDFs off your board.

What to do:


Confirm the attachment is the actual RC, not a cover email, invoice, or unrelated document.

If it really is a rate confirmation that wasn't picked up, bring it in with File Upload, or key the load in manually.


The email arrived somewhere Numeo isn't watching

Email extraction only reads rate confirmations from your connected inbox. If the RC landed on a different address or account, Numeo never saw it.

What to do:


Forward it into the connected inbox, or

Add it directly with File Upload.


Good to know


One real rate confirmation makes one load — resending the same email won't stack duplicates, by design.

When in doubt on a stuck RC, support can look at why a specific file didn't process.


Need a hand? Email support@numeo.ai or use the in-app Help option.PreviousNumeo One FAQNextA truck isn't reporting or is missing from the map

Numeo One FAQ
Quick answers on supported ELDs, plans and the free trial, the multi-company cap, whether you need an ELD, and how drivers get updates.
3 min read

Short answers to the questions dispatchers ask most when they're getting started with Numeo One. For anything deeper, follow the links to the full article.

Which ELDs does Numeo One support?

Samsara, Motive, and 15+ more. If your drivers already run a device and portal for Hours of Service, there's a good chance it's on the list. See Connect your ELD, or browse the integrations directory for the current set.

Do I need an ELD to use Numeo One?

No. You can import loads, assign trucks and drivers, invoice, and run pay without one. Connecting an ELD is what turns on the automated side — live location, ETA, geofence arrival and departure, and Hours of Service. Without it you can still run loads and update status by hand.

What plans are there, and is there a free trial?

Numeo One is billed per truck in three plans — Basic, Pro, and Enterprise — and yes, there's a free trial. Start with "Get Started free". If there's no payment method on file when the trial ends, the subscription cancels on its own. See Plans, billing, and integrations and the pricing page.

How many companies (MCs) can I run in one account?

Up to 5 companies in one organization. Each needs its own MC — a duplicate MC is rejected. You can filter loads by company or MC across the board. See Managing multiple companies (multi-MC).

How do my drivers get updates?

Over Telegram. Drivers get their load assignment and automatic status updates there — no separate login to keep up with. Your internal team can be reached over Telegram or email. See Driver notifications over Telegram.

Something's not working — where do I look?


A rate confirmation didn't become a load → RateCon not creating a load.

A truck's missing from the map or HOS is stale → ELD not reporting or truck missing.

Status or a tracking link isn't updating → Status and tracking not updating.

An invoice or billing issue → Invoice and billing issues.

Importing loadsPower user
RateCon deduplication and reprocessing
Why the same rate confirmation won't create a duplicate load — the fingerprint, the 24-hour window, and how to reprocess.
4 min read

Brokers resend rate confirmations all the time — a forward here, a reply there, the same file twice. Numeo One makes sure you get one load per real rate confirmation, not one per email. This is the deeper look at how that works and what to do when you actually want a file re-read.

How duplicate detection works

When a rate confirmation comes in, Numeo doesn't just look at the filename — it fingerprints the file itself.


It takes a fingerprint of the rate confirmation's contents and ties it to the account it came in on.

If a rate confirmation with the same fingerprint shows up again within a 24-hour window, Numeo treats it as one it already handled and skips it — no duplicate load.

After the window passes, that fingerprint is no longer held, so a genuinely new send can come through.


The result is that resends, replies, and forwards of a confirmation you've already got don't clutter your board.

"Not a rate confirmation" results

Not every attachment is a rate confirmation, and Numeo won't turn a random document into a load.


If the AI reads a PDF and decides it isn't a rate confirmation, it returns a "not a RateCon" result and no load is created.

That's expected — a broker packet, an invoice, or an unrelated PDF simply won't become a load.


Reprocessing the same file

Duplicate protection is a deliberate tradeoff: it stops duplicates, which also means the exact same file won't be re-read within its window. If a load didn't land the way you expected:


Check the board first. The load may already be there under Rate Confirmation — look before you resend.

If the details changed, update the existing load rather than resending the same file. Editing the load you have is cleaner than fighting the fingerprint.

If you genuinely need it re-read, wait out the 24-hour window so the new send doesn't collide with the earlier copy, or reach out to support.

Rate confirmation email extraction
How Numeo reads rate confirmations from your connected email, skips duplicates, and turns them into loads.
4 min read

When a broker emails you a rate confirmation, Numeo One reads it and builds the load for you. No copy-paste, no re-keying stops and rates. The load shows up on your board with the source Rate Confirmation, ready to assign.

How it works

Once your email is connected, Numeo watches for rate confirmations coming in:


A broker sends you an RC by email.

Numeo picks up the message and looks at the attachment.

The AI recognizes it as a rate confirmation and reads out the details — broker, stops, rate, reference numbers.

A new load is created on your board, geocoded and marked as Rate Confirmation.


Attachments that aren't rate confirmations are skipped — a random PDF that isn't an RC won't turn into a load.


Animated demo
A rate confirmation email becoming a load
A short screen recording will be added here.

Duplicate protection

Brokers resend. A confirmation gets forwarded, replied to, or sent twice — and you don't want two copies of the same load. Numeo guards against that automatically:


It fingerprints each rate confirmation and checks it against what's already come in.

If the same rate confirmation shows up again within a 24-hour window, Numeo skips it instead of creating a duplicate load.


You get one load per real rate confirmation, not one per email.

Reprocessing the same rate confirmation

Because of that duplicate protection, sending the exact same rate confirmation file again within the 24-hour window won't create a new load — Numeo treats it as the one it already handled.

If a load didn't come through the way you expected:


Check the board first — the load may already be there under Rate Confirmation.

If the details changed, the cleaner path is to update the existing load rather than resend the same file.

If you genuinely need it re-read, wait out the window or reach out to support so it doesn't collide with the earlier copy.


Good to know


Reading from email is the most hands-off way to get loads in — connect the inbox once and new RCs flow onto the board on their own.

If a rate confirmation arrives somewhere Numeo isn't watching, you can still bring it in with File Upload.

Settings & integrationsIntermediate
Manage your subscription and billing
Change your plan, adjust truck seats, update your card in the Stripe customer portal, and see how the free trial converts.
3 min read

Numeo One bills per truck through Stripe. Once you're subscribed, you manage the whole thing yourself — plan, truck count, payment method, and past invoices — from the Stripe customer portal. No email back-and-forth to change a plan.

Manage everything in the Stripe portal

Your subscription is handled in the Stripe customer portal. From there you can:


Update your card or payment method.

Change your plan — switch between Basic and Pro yourself. Enterprise is custom, so talk to us to move onto it.

Adjust your truck count — add or remove seats as your fleet changes.

View past invoices and receipts.


Billing is per truck, so your bill scales with the number of trucks you're running.

How the free trial converts

New accounts can start on a free trial with "Get Started free". When the trial ends:


If a payment method is on file, the subscription starts and you're billed for your plan and truck count.

If there's no payment method on file, the subscription cancels on its own — no surprise charge.


So you can try Numeo One without committing a card, and nothing bills you silently.

Change your truck count

Because pricing is per truck, adjusting seats is how your bill tracks your fleet. Add trucks when you grow; drop them when equipment leaves. Seat changes are made in the portal and reflected on your next invoice.

Good to know


For what each plan includes and the per-truck prices, see Plans, billing, and integrations and the pricing page.

Not sure which plan fits your fleet? Choose "Book a Demo".

Running a larger fleet (100+ trucks)? Enterprise is custom — talk to us.

The ongoing loads board
Your live board of running loads — filter by company or broker, read each load's status, and watch loads move from En Route to Completed.
3 min read

The ongoing loads board is your live view of everything on the road. Every assigned load shows up here with its current status, and it updates itself as trucks move — so a glance tells you what's en route, what's sitting at a stop, and what's done.


Screenshot
The ongoing loads board
A product screenshot will be added here.

Read a load's status

Each load carries a status that walks through the trip:

En Route → Arrived → Completed

Numeo sets these automatically from the truck's geofence — "Arrived" once it's held a stop for 10 minutes, "Completed" when the load wraps — or you can set a status by hand. For the full mechanics, see Live tracking, ETA, and geofences.

Filter the board

When the board is full, filters get you to the loads you care about:


Company / MC — if you run more than one authority, filter to just one so you're only looking at its loads.

Broker — keep preferred and blocked broker lists so the brokers you work with (and the ones you don't) are easy to spot and sort.


Where loads come from

Loads land on the board once they're assigned on the scheduler. See Using the scheduler and dispatch board for assigning trucks and drivers.

Coming soon

A couple of board upgrades are rolling out:


Column controls — show and hide columns so the board matches how you dispatch.

Dark mode for the board.


If you don't see these yet, they're on the way.

Good to know


The board is live — status changes and locations update on their own as your ELD reports in, so you don't have to refresh to see the latest.

Dispatch & schedulingPower user
Assignment overlaps and driver availability
How overlap confirmation, batch-applied suggestions, and driver-status blocks keep double-bookings and off-road drivers off the board.
4 min read

When you assign a truck that's already busy — or a driver who's off the road — Numeo One stops you before it books. This page covers exactly how overlap confirmation and driver-status blocks work, and how to batch through suggestions when you're clearing a stack of loads.

Overlap confirmation

When you drop a truck onto a load and that truck is already committed in the same window, Numeo surfaces the overlap and asks you to confirm before it books over it. Nothing double-books silently.

From there you have two choices:


Confirm — you meant to move it, so Numeo books the new assignment over the old window.

Back out — pick a different truck instead.


This is a confirmation, not a hard block: an overlap is sometimes exactly what you want, so Numeo makes sure you saw it and lets you decide.

Batch-applying smart suggestions

When several loads need trucks at once, Numeo does the first pass for you:


Smart suggestions recommend which truck fits which load. They load on the ongoing-loads board so you're reacting to a shortlist instead of a blank board.

Overlap suggestions can be applied in a batch — clear a stack of loads in one move rather than confirming each one by hand.


You still make the final call; the suggestions just get you most of the way there.

Driver-status blocks

Every driver is active, inactive, or terminated, and that status decides whether they can be assigned at all:


Active — assigns normally.

Inactive or terminated — blocked, and the block can't be overridden.


Unlike a truck overlap — which you can confirm through — an inactive or terminated driver is a hard stop. A driver who's off the road can't accidentally end up on a load, no matter how you try to assign them.

Power tips


Setting a driver's status (including a Driver Termination Date) keeps them out of future assignments automatically — you don't have to remember to exclude them. See Driver and truck profiles.

Overlap and availability checks run inside the same drag-and-drop flow you already use — see Using the scheduler and dispatch board.

Settings & integrationsIntermediate
The integrations directory
Browse everything you can connect to Numeo One — ELD, factoring, toll and fuel, trailer GPS, and TMS accounts — and what each turns on.
4 min read

Numeo One connects to the tools you already run — your ELD, factoring company, fuel and toll cards, trailer GPS, and another TMS. The full list lives in the integrations directory, and you connect each one from Settings. This article walks the categories and what turning each on does for you.

The categories

The directory is grouped the same way the in-product Settings are:


ELD — Samsara, Motive, and 15+ more.

Factoring — RTS, Triumph, PRO Funding, WEX, Stratopay, Outgo, TAFS, and others.

Toll & Fuel — BestPass, PrePass, and Relay Payments.

Trailer GPS — Phillips Connect and other trailer telematics.

Account Integrations — connect a DITAT or QuickManage TMS account.


What each turns on

Each connection lights up a different part of Numeo One:


ELD turns on live tracking, the fleet map, ETA, geofence arrival and departure, and Hours of Service. It's the connection most of the tracking features run on. See Connect your ELD.

Factoring lets you submit invoices automatically and track payment. See Connect your factoring company.

Toll & Fuel brings toll costs into pay and accounting and feeds fuel-card reconciliation. See Fuel tracking and reconciliation.

Trailer GPS adds trailer location on top of the truck's ELD feed.

Account Integrations mirror dispatch and loads from another TMS. See Connect an external TMS (DITAT, QuickManage).


Connect one


Open Settings and find the integration category.

Pick the provider from the list.

Enter the account credentials or details it asks for to link it.


Connecting an ELD and your factoring company are the first two cards on your setup checklist, so they're worth doing early.

Good to know


Accounting software connects here too — see Connect QuickBooks.

The set of live providers can change as we add more; the integrations directory always shows the current list.

Some integrations may depend on your plan — check the pricing page.

Driver communicationIntermediate
Load-assignment messages and the tracking link
Edit the message your driver gets when you assign a load, pick the tracking link to include, and let it adapt to the load's stage.
3 min read

When you assign a load to a driver, Numeo One sends them a Telegram message with the load details. You get to review and edit that message before it goes out — and decide whether to include a live tracking link.

Assign the load and open the message

The message editor opens as part of assigning a load:


Assign the load to a truck and driver on the scheduler or the Ongoing Loads board. See Using the scheduler and dispatch board.

The load-assignment message opens with the load details filled in — stops, times, references.

Review the wording and adjust anything you want the driver to see.

Choose whether to include a tracking link.

Send.



Screenshot
The load-assignment message editor
A product screenshot will be added here.

The message adapts to the load's stage

The template knows where the load is. So the driver sees the right wording whether the load is still en route or has already arrived at a stop — you don't keep separate messages for each case. Assign, update, and unassign each send their own note so the driver always has the current picture.

Include a tracking link

From the same editor you can attach a live tracking link. The link lets the recipient follow the truck's location and ETA without logging in, and it expires on its own when the load completes or cancels. The full walkthrough — including sharing it with a broker — is in Share a live tracking link with brokers.

Good to know


Who the message and later alerts go to is set separately — see Notification recipients and templates.

Pulling the broker's pickup and delivery instructions from the Rate Confirmation into the message — as a template variable — is coming soon.

Tracking & ETAIntermediate
Live tracking, ETA, and geofences
How Numeo One tracks loads live, keeps ETA current with auto-recalc, and detects arrival and departure at each stop.
4 min read

Once your ELD is connected, every load tracks itself. Numeo One follows the truck live, keeps the ETA up to date as the route changes, and marks each stop as arrived or departed on its own — so you're not calling the driver to ask where they are.


Screenshot
A load tracking live with its ETA and geofence status
A product screenshot will be added here.

Live location

Truck locations refresh every 30 seconds through your connected ELD. If you haven't linked one yet, start with Connect your ELD — tracking runs on that feed.

ETA and auto-recalc

Numeo calculates each load's ETA from the truck's live position to the next stop. The ETA isn't a one-time guess — it recalculates automatically when the truck deviates from the planned route, so the number you're looking at reflects where the truck actually is. As the truck gets close to a stop, Numeo tightens the estimate again.

Geofences: arrival and departure

Every stop has a geofence — a 1-mile radius around it. Numeo watches when the truck enters and leaves that circle to move the load's status without anyone typing it in.


Nearby Stop Detection fires the moment the truck first enters the stop's geofence — a heads-up that it's close.

Arrival is confirmed once the truck stays inside the geofence for at least 10 minutes. That short wait filters out a truck just passing through, so "Arrived" means arrived.

Departure Detection fires after the truck leaves the geofence.


On the load, a "Geofence" countdown shows how long the truck has been sitting inside the stop before arrival is confirmed.


Animated demo
The geofence countdown on a stop
A short screen recording will be added here.

Load statuses

As a load moves, its status walks through:

En Route → Arrived → Completed

Numeo can set these automatically from the geofence, or you can set them by hand when you need to. Each status change is recorded with how it happened — automatically from the geofence, on a schedule, or manually — so you always know whether the board updated itself or someone touched it.

Keep the broker in the loop

You can share a login-free link that shows the broker this same live location and ETA, without giving them an account. See Share a live tracking link with brokers.

Good to know


Tracking and status detection run continuously in the background — you don't have to refresh or re-arm anything per load.

Arrival, nearby, and departure events can also send alerts to your team, the driver, or the broker. See Driver notifications over Telegram for how those alerts get turned on and routed.

Getting startedBeginner
Getting started with Numeo One
What Numeo One is — an AI TMS that runs booking to payments in one workspace — and the checklist to set it up.
3 min read

Numeo One is an AI-native TMS for carriers. It runs your operation from booking to payments in one workspace — import loads, assign trucks and drivers, track live, message drivers, and invoice and get paid. No jumping between a load board, a spreadsheet, and three other tools.


Screenshot
The Numeo One setup checklist
A product screenshot will be added here.

What Numeo One does

Once you're set up, the day's work lives in one place:


Import loads from your email, a file, an external TMS, Amazon Relay, or by hand. See Importing loads: the five sources.

Assign and dispatch trucks and drivers on the scheduler and the ongoing-loads board.

Track live with ETA, geofence arrival and departure, and a login-free tracking link you can share with a broker.

Message drivers with Telegram and email alerts — delays, arrivals, wakeup calls, and more.

Bill and get paid with invoicing, driver and contractor pay, and factoring submission.


The AI does the repetitive first pass — reading rate confirmations, updating status, following up. You stay in control and make the call.

Set up your account

After you create your account at agent.numeo.ai, a short setup checklist walks you through the essentials. Work through it in order:


Add your MC number. FMCSA fills in your company details for you. See Add your MC and company.

Connect ELD. Link Samsara, Motive, AT ELD, or another ELD to get live truck locations and Hours of Service data.

Connect Factoring. Link your factoring company for automatic invoice submission and faster payment tracking.

Invite Teammate. Bring your dispatchers in and set what each can do. See Invite and manage your team.


You don't have to finish all of it before you start booking — but ELD and factoring are what turn on live tracking and faster payments, so they're worth doing early.

Good to know


Short in-app tutorials cover the main areas: Fleet, Safety, Accounting, and Updater (the AI status updater).

Numeo One is billed per truck, and you can start on a free trial. See the pricing page for plans and what each includes.


Need a hand? Email support@numeo.ai or use the in-app Help option.NextAdd your MC and company

Troubleshooting & FAQIntermediate
Status or tracking isn't updating
Arrival or departure isn't firing, ETA looks off, or a broker's tracking link is dead — geofence dwell, ETA recalc, manual status, and expired links.
4 min read

A load's status isn't moving, the ETA looks stale, or a broker says their tracking link is dead. Most of these trace back to how geofences, ETA, and tracking links work — here's what's normal and what to check.

Arrival or departure isn't firing

Numeo sets status from the stop's geofence — a 1-mile radius around each stop.


Arrival isn't confirmed the instant the truck rolls in. The truck has to stay inside the geofence for about 10 minutes first, so a drive-by doesn't trigger a false arrival. On the load, the "Geofence" countdown shows how long it's been sitting. If the truck just got there, give it the dwell.

Nearby Stop Detection fires when the truck first enters the geofence; Departure fires after it leaves. If none of these move, check that live location is flowing — see A truck isn't reporting or is missing from the map.


You can always set a status by hand when you need to. Each change is recorded with how it happened — automatically from the geofence, on a schedule, or manually — so you can tell whether the board updated itself or someone touched it.

See Live tracking, ETA, and geofences for the full picture.

The ETA looks off

The ETA recalculates from the truck's live position, and it auto-recalcs when the truck deviates from the planned route. If it looks stale:


Confirm live location is current — a stalled ELD feed means a stalled ETA.

Give it a beat after a route change; the number catches up as fresh positions come in and tightens as the truck nears the stop.


A broker's tracking link is dead

Tracking links are tied to the load and expire on their own when the load is completed or cancelled — that's by design, so old links don't keep leaking location after the job's done.


If the load is finished, the link is supposed to be dead. Generate a fresh link only for an active load.

Each link is per load, so working several loads with one broker means several links. See Share a live tracking link with brokers.


Good to know


Tracking and status detection run continuously in the background — there's nothing to refresh or re-arm per load.

If status still won't move with a healthy ELD feed and the dwell met, support can look at the specific load.

Troubleshooting & FAQIntermediate
Invoice and billing issues
Known invoicing snags — data not extracted on upload, an invoice number changing after an undo — plus factoring submission checks.
3 min read

Invoicing pulls from the load, so most issues come down to the load data behind the invoice or the factoring connection in front of it. Here's what to check for the common ones.

Invoice data didn't come through on upload

If you uploaded an invoice and the data didn't get extracted the way you expected, the numbers on the invoice may not match the source document.


Re-check the invoice against the load it was built from — the rate, stops, and reference numbers come from the load.

If a value looks wrong or blank, correct it on the invoice before you send.

Extracting data cleanly from uploaded invoices is an area we're actively improving, so if a specific upload won't parse, send it to support and we'll look.


An invoice number changed after an undo

If you undo or revert a change and notice the invoice number shifted, note the current number before you send or submit, so what the broker or your factoring company receives matches your records. Invoice-number stability on undo/revert is a known area under active work — flag any case to support with the load and the numbers you saw.

A factoring submission didn't go through

If you submitted an invoice to your factoring company and it didn't land:


Confirm your factoring provider is still connected — check the Connect Factoring setup or Settings. See Connect your factoring company.

Watch the invoice's status, filters, and notes on the factoring dashboard under Accounting → Factoring. See Factoring submission and tracking.

Make sure the invoice itself is complete before submitting — a missing or mismatched value can hold up a submission.


Good to know


Invoicing basics — create, export, and email an invoice from a completed load — are in Invoicing and getting paid.

Chasing what's overdue is a separate flow — see Invoice ageing and follow-up.


Need a hand? Email support@numeo.ai or use the in-app Help option.PreviousStatus or tracking isn't updating

Upload or create a load manually
Upload a rate confirmation or file, or type a load in by hand when there's no email to read.
3 min read

Not every load arrives in a watched inbox. Sometimes you've got the rate confirmation as a PDF, and sometimes you've got no paperwork at all — just the details in your head. Numeo One covers both: upload the file and let the AI read it, or type the load in by hand.

Upload a rate confirmation or file

When the RC didn't come through a connected inbox, you can hand it to Numeo directly.


Open the load import option and choose to upload a file.

Pick the rate confirmation PDF or file from your computer.

Numeo reads it the same way it reads emailed RCs and builds the load.


The load lands on your board with the source File Upload, geocoded and ready to assign.


Screenshot
Uploading a rate confirmation file
A product screenshot will be added here.

Enter a load by hand

When there's no document at all, create the load yourself with Manual Entry:


Start a new load and choose to enter it manually.

Fill in the broker, the pickup and delivery stops, the rate, and any reference numbers.

Save it — it shows up on the board tagged Manual Entry.


Manually entered stops are placed on the map just like every other source, so ETA and geofence tracking work right away.

Which one should I use?


Have the RC as a file? Use File Upload so the AI does the typing.

No paperwork at all? Use Manual Entry and key in the details.


For the hands-off path where Numeo reads RCs straight from your inbox, see Rate confirmation email extraction. For the full list of ways loads come in, see Importing loads: the five sources.

Tracking & ETAIntermediate
Geofence arrival and departure detection
How the 1-mile stop geofence and the 10-minute arrival dwell let a load mark itself arrived and departed on its own.
4 min read

Numeo One draws a circle around every stop and watches the truck cross it. That's how a load marks itself arrived and departed without you calling the driver to ask.


Screenshot
A stop geofence with the arrival countdown
A product screenshot will be added here.

The stop geofence

Every stop on a load gets a geofence — a 1-mile radius around the stop location. Numeo compares the truck's live position to that circle continuously and reacts as the truck crosses in and out.

The three detection events

Numeo watches for three things at each stop:


Nearby Stop Detection — fires the moment the truck first crosses into the geofence. It's your heads-up that the truck is close.

Arrival Detection — fires after the truck has stayed inside the geofence for at least 10 minutes.

Departure Detection — fires once the truck leaves the geofence.


Why arrival waits 10 minutes

The 10-minute dwell filters out a truck that's just passing by or caught at a light near the stop. Making the truck settle for a few minutes means "Arrived" actually means arrived, not "drove past."

On the load, a "Geofence" countdown shows how long the truck has been sitting inside the stop before arrival is confirmed — so you can watch it count down.


Animated demo
The geofence countdown on a stop
A short screen recording will be added here.

How the status changes

As the truck crosses these boundaries, the load's status moves through En Route → Arrived → Completed. Numeo can set those from the geofence automatically, on a schedule, or you can set one by hand — and every change records which way it happened. For the full breakdown, see Load statuses explained.

Turn detections into alerts

Each of these events can also notify the people who need to know — your team, the driver, or the broker. Arrival, nearby-stop, and departure alerts are part of the notification catalog. See Driver notifications over Telegram.

Good to know


ETA reacts to the geofence too: as the truck nears the 1-mile boundary, Numeo re-tightens the ETA so the number stays honest. See Live tracking, ETA, and geofences.

Detection runs in the background on every load — you don't arm or refresh anything per stop.

Troubleshooting & FAQIntermediate
A truck isn't reporting or is missing from the map
A truck isn't on the fleet map or its Hours of Service is stale — check the ELD connection, the 30-second update cadence, and the ELD Offline Alert.
3 min read

A truck's not showing on the fleet map, or its Hours of Service looks stale. Live location and HOS both come from your connected ELD, so troubleshooting starts there.

How location is supposed to flow

Truck locations refresh about every 30 seconds through your connected ELD. That feed drives the fleet map, live tracking, ETA, and geofence detection. If the feed stops, everything downstream goes quiet for that truck.

Walk through these checks


Is the ELD connected? Open Settings and confirm the ELD integration is still linked and its credentials are current. A connection that dropped or expired stops the feed. See Connect your ELD.

Is the truck assigned and pulled in? Numeo imports trucks and drivers from the ELD. A truck that isn't in the ELD's vehicle data, or isn't assigned to a driver, may not appear. Re-check the import and assignments.

Is the device itself reporting? If the ELD hardware is off, unplugged, or out of coverage, no location comes through — nothing on the Numeo side can fill that gap.

Give it a cycle. Updates land roughly every 30 seconds, so a brand-new connection or a truck just powered on may take a moment to show.


Let Numeo tell you next time

Turn on the ELD Offline Alert so you're not the one noticing a truck went dark. When a truck's ELD stops reporting location, Numeo messages the driver so it gets fixed fast — this alert always goes to the driver only. See Driver notifications over Telegram.

Good to know


No ELD on that truck yet? It won't appear on the live map — you can still run its loads and update status by hand.

Once the feed is back, live location, ETA, and geofence detection pick up on their own. See Live tracking, ETA, and geofences.

Driver communicationIntermediate
Notification recipients and templates
Choose who gets each alert — driver, dispatcher, broker, or a custom group — and edit the load-assignment message your driver sees.
4 min read

Every alert in Numeo One can go to different people, and the message your driver gets when you assign a load is yours to edit. This article covers the recipient toggles and the load-assignment message template.

Pick who gets each alert

Each alert has its own recipient toggles, so the right people hear about the right thing:


Driver — the assigned driver, over Telegram.

Dispatcher — the dispatcher on the load.

Broker — the broker, for updates you want to share outward.

Custom Group — a group you define, for anyone else who should be looped in.

Internal Team — your own team channel, over Telegram or email.


Toggle any combination per alert. For example, keep the ELD Offline Alert to the driver only (it's driver-only by design), send Arrival Detection to the broker, and route the Detention Alert to your team.

Two extra toggles show up where they help:


Reply All — keep everyone on the thread in the loop on a reply.

Exclude Delay — on Send Update, leave delay notices out of the routine status updates.


The load-assignment message

When you assign a load to a driver, Numeo One sends them a message with the load details. You edit that message before it goes out:


Assign the load to a truck and driver on the scheduler or the Ongoing Loads board.

In the message editor, review the load details and adjust the wording.

Choose whether to include a tracking link.

Send.


The message adapts to the load's stage, so the driver sees the right wording whether the load is en route or already arrived.

Good to know


The internal team channel can be Telegram or email; driver and broker messages go over Telegram.

Choosing who receives an alert is separate from turning it on — enable the alerts first in Driver notifications over Telegram.

Want the driver to see the broker's pickup and delivery instructions in the message? Reading those instructions from the Rate Confirmation into the template is coming soon.


Need a hand? Email support@numeo.ai or use the in-app Help option.PreviousSafety, speed, and equipment alertsNextLoad-assignment messages and the tracking link

Importing loadsBeginner
Importing loads — the five sources
Every load in Numeo One comes in through one of five sources. Here's what each is and when to use it.
3 min read

Every load in Numeo One comes in through one of five sources. Whichever you use, the load lands on the same board — with the pickup and delivery already placed on the map — ready to assign and track.

The five load sources


Rate Confirmation — the AI reads the rate confirmation straight from your connected email and builds the load for you. This is the hands-off path. See Rate confirmation email extraction.

File Upload — you upload a rate confirmation PDF or file yourself, and the AI reads it the same way. See Upload or create a load manually.

TMS — loads sync in from an external TMS you already run, like DITAT or QuickManage. See Connect an external TMS.

Amazon Relay — your Relay trips come onto the board and stay in sync. See Import Amazon Relay loads.

Manual Entry — you type a load in by hand when there's no document to read. See Upload or create a load manually.


Each load shows its source, so you always know where it came from.

Every source lands on the same board

No matter how a load gets in, it behaves the same once it's there:


It's geocoded — pickup and delivery are placed on the map, so ETA and geofence tracking work right away.

It shows up on your ongoing-loads board, where you filter by company or MC and assign a truck and driver.


Which source should I use?


Most of your loads arrive by email? Connect your inbox and let Rate Confirmation do the work.

Got the RC as a PDF but not in a watched inbox? Use File Upload.

Already running DITAT, QuickManage, or Amazon Relay? Connect it and let loads sync in.

No paperwork at all? Use Manual Entry.

Importing loadsPower user
Connect an external TMS (DITAT, QuickManage)
Connect DITAT or QuickManage, import trips and invoices by CSV or Excel, and sync loads onto your board.
4 min read

Already running another TMS? You don't have to start from scratch. Numeo One connects to DITAT and QuickManage, so your existing trips and invoices come across and land on the same board as everything else — tagged with the source TMS.

Connecting an external TMS may depend on your plan. See the pricing page for what's included.

Providers you can connect

Numeo One imports from these external systems today:


DITAT

QuickManage


You'll find them in the load import options, alongside Amazon Relay.

Import by file

The most direct way to bring loads over is to export from your current system and import the file into Numeo:


DITAT trips / shipments — export the trips or shipments CSV from DITAT and import it. Numeo reads the export and creates the loads.

QuickManage customers / Data Truck — import the Excel export. Numeo sniffs the header row and figures out which export it is, so you don't have to tell it.



Screenshot
Importing a DITAT CSV export
A product screenshot will be added here.

Bring your invoices too

You can also import an invoices export from DITAT, QuickManage, or Data Truck. Those come in as broker invoices, so your billing picks up where your old system left off.

Keep loads in sync

Beyond a one-time file import, Numeo can sync with the connected provider so loads stay current as they change on the other side:


Run a sync to pull the latest from the provider.

Numeo shows you what it found so you can review before you apply — nothing gets pushed onto your board blindly.

Apply the changes you want, and your loads update.


Good to know


Imported loads behave like any other Numeo load once they're on the board — geocoded, filterable by company or MC, and ready to assign and track.

Not sure a provider fits your export? Reach out to support before a big import and we'll point you at the right file.


For Amazon Relay specifically, see Import Amazon Relay loads. For all the ways loads come in, see Importing loads: the five sources.

Invoice ageing and follow-up
Read the ageing view, work the oldest unpaid invoices first, and let Numeo help draft accounting follow-ups on what's overdue.
3 min read

Once invoices go out, the job is getting them paid. The Invoices page shows ageing so you can see what's current and what's overdue at a glance, and Numeo can help you chase the ones that have gone quiet. Invoices live under Accounting → Invoices.

Sending an invoice in the first place is covered in Invoicing and getting paid.

Read the ageing view

The Invoices page groups what's owed by how long it's been outstanding — current versus past due — so you're not scanning a flat list. Sort and filter to bring the oldest unpaid invoices to the top and work those first.


Screenshot
The invoices page showing ageing
A product screenshot will be added here.

Chase what's overdue

For an invoice that's aged past your terms:


Filter to past-due invoices and start with the oldest.

Open the invoice to check the broker, amount, and reference numbers.

Send a follow-up to the broker — Numeo's accounting assistant can help draft the follow-up so you're editing, not writing from scratch.

Note anything you learn (promised pay date, dispute) so the next person sees it.


You stay in control of what goes out — Numeo does the first pass, you send.

Good to know


If you factor your invoices, submitting to your factoring company is a faster route to cash than chasing the broker — see Factoring submission and tracking.

Support for a custom remit-to address per invoice is rolling out — coming soon.

Importing loadsIntermediate
Bills of lading and load paperwork
Where BOL and POD sit on a load, how Numeo flags missing paperwork, and how BOL weight feeds the Heavy Load Alert.
3 min read

Every load carries paperwork — the bill of lading (BOL) at pickup, the proof of delivery (POD) at the end. Numeo One keeps that paperwork with the load, flags when a required document is missing, and reads the BOL weight so you know when a load is heavy.

Paperwork on a load

The documents for a load — like the BOL and POD — live with the load itself, so the whole trip's paperwork stays in one place instead of scattered across your inbox.

Missing-paperwork detection

You don't have to remember which loads are still missing a document. Numeo can watch for it and let you know.


The Missing Paperwork alert fires when a required document — like the BOL or POD — is missing for a load.

Turn it on per load and route it wherever you want, alongside your other alerts. See Driver notifications on Telegram.


BOL weight and the Heavy Load Alert

Numeo reads the total weight off the BOL, which feeds the Heavy Load Alert.


When a load's total BOL weight goes over your threshold — 42,000 lbs by default — the Heavy Load Alert fires.

Adjust the threshold to match how you want to be warned about heavy freight.


Good to know

Deeper AI reading of load documents — recognizing and checking paperwork automatically — is in the works. For now, Numeo keeps the paperwork on the load, flags what's missing, and reads the BOL weight as described above.

Related

Driver notifications on Telegram — set up the Missing Paperwork and Heavy Load alerts.

Getting startedBeginner
What is Numeo Spot?
Numeo Spot is a free Chrome extension that adds broker checks, profit math, one-click emails, and calling right inside DAT and Truckstop.
3 min read

Numeo Spot is a free Chrome extension for dispatchers and carriers. It works inside DAT and Truckstop — the load boards you already use — and adds the tools you normally juggle across a dozen tabs: broker and factoring checks, real profit math, one-click broker emails, and calling. Less tab-switching. Faster booking.


Screenshot
The Numeo Spot toolbar on a DAT load board
A product screenshot will be added here.

What it does

Numeo Spot layers onto the load board so you can work a load without leaving it:


Find loads — search the same load across 15+ boards, and let Load Radar watch your DAT search around the clock.

Vet the broker — see factoring and credit status right on the row, and check real profit, RPM, and deadhead before you reach out.

Work the load — email the broker in one click with your templates and signature, copy the MC and load details, and call from the board.


You stay in control the whole time. Numeo does the repetitive first pass — you make the call.

Where it runs

Spot's full toolbar shows up on DAT and Truckstop. It also pulls loads from 15+ broker and carrier portals (Amazon Relay, C.H. Robinson, TQL, RXO, Uber Freight, JB Hunt, and more) so you can compare the same lane in one place. See Search a load on more boards.

Free vs Pro

Spot is free to install and use. The free plan covers the core: load search, factoring checks, the profit calculator, and a daily allowance of broker emails. Pro adds the heavier tools — Load Radar, toll routes, your Recent broker outreach, and higher email limits. See the full breakdown on the pricing page.

Get started


Install the Chrome extension.

Sign in and connect your email.

Open DAT or Truckstop and take the side-panel and toolbar tour.

Finding loadsIntermediate
Set up Load Radar
Load Radar watches your DAT search around the clock and forwards matching loads straight to your Telegram or email.
3 min read

Load Radar watches this DAT search 24/7 and can forward matching loads to your Telegram or email. Set your filters once, pick where you want the alerts, and let it run while you work other lanes — no refreshing, no watching the board.

Load Radar is a Pro feature and works on DAT only. See the pricing page for what's included.

Set it up in three steps

Open the Load Radar tab in the side panel over your DAT search, then:


Set your filters.

Pick a notification channel.

Tap Start Radar.



Animated demo
Setting Load Radar filters
A short screen recording will be added here.

1. Set your filters

Load Radar only forwards loads that match what you tell it to look for. Fill in whichever fields matter for this lane — you don't need all of them:


Min Rate — lowest total rate you'll take.

Min RPM — lowest rate per mile (for example, 1.80).

Min Miles / Max Miles — trip length range.

Max Deadhead — how far you'll drive empty to the pickup.

Min Weight / Max Weight — the weight range you can haul.

Max Length — longest load you'll run.

Broker MC blacklist — MC numbers to skip so those brokers never trigger an alert.


You need at least one filter set for Radar to start.

2. Pick a notification channel

Choose where matches land. You can turn on more than one:


Telegram — connect your Telegram once, then receive messages for matching loads.

Email — send to one or more addresses.

Push — mobile push notifications. This one needs the Numeo mobile app installed; a QR code shows up to help you install it.


3. Tap Start Radar

Hit Start Radar and it begins watching this DAT search. The button switches to Stop Radar — tap it any time to turn the watch off.

If the button is greyed out

Radar tells you why it can't start yet. Common reasons:


No active DAT search — run a search on the board first.

Fill at least one filter field — add a rate, RPM, or another filter.

Enable at least one notification channel — pick Telegram, email, or push.

Connect Telegram first — link your Telegram before choosing it as a channel.

Install the mobile app first — needed before push alerts will send.


Good to know


Each Radar is tied to the DAT search you set it up on. Change the search and set up a fresh Radar for the new lane.

The Radar keeps running in the background — you don't have to keep the side panel open.

It's DAT-only and hidden on Truckstop.


To search a single load across more boards instead of watching one lane, see Search a load on more boards. To tidy up the board before you set filters, see Clean up your board with smart filters.

Need a hand? Email support@numeo.ai or use the Help button in the side panel.PreviousRead your Load Hub resultsNextLoad Radar notification channels

Troubleshooting & FAQPower user
Troubleshooting
Quick fixes for the side panel, sign-in, your load board, and email in Numeo Spot — plus how to reach support.
4 min read

Most Spot hiccups clear up in a step or two. Find your symptom below and try the fix. Still stuck? Support contacts are at the bottom.

The side panel won't open, or there's no Numeo button


Make sure you're on a supported board. The full toolbar only shows on DAT and Truckstop.

Refresh the board tab. Spot auto-updates, so if a tab was open during an update, reloading it brings the new version in.

Confirm the extension is enabled and pinned. See Install Numeo Spot.

Confirm you're signed in. See Sign in and connect email.


No loads are showing on the board


Loads come from your active DAT or Truckstop search — run a search first.

Check your smart filters. Hiding Canada or Mexico, excluding states, a high Min Rate or Min RPM, or Hide duplicates can empty the board.

Refresh the board, or toggle Auto-refresh off and on.


Truckstop isn't responding


Some tabs are hidden on Truckstop by design — Load Radar and Recent are DAT-only, so not seeing them there is expected.

Refresh the Truckstop tab and confirm you're on main.truckstop.com.

If actions still don't fire, sign out and back in.


"Continue with Google" won't sign me in

Sign-in fails most often when the method doesn't match how the account was created:


Use the same method you signed up with. If you registered with email and password, sign in that way instead of a provider button — and vice versa. Google accounts use Continue with Google; Outlook accounts use Continue with Microsoft.

Account made in the mobile app? Those have no password yet. As Spot tells you: "This account was created via the mobile app and does not have a password. Use Google or Outlook sign-in below, or click 'Forgot Password?'" Pick Continue with Google or Continue with Microsoft, or use Forgot Password? to set one.


More detail in Sign in and connect email.

The side panel won't open in a browser other than Chrome

Spot is built for Chrome and uses Chrome's built-in side panel. Other browsers don't all support that side panel the same way, so it may not open. Use Google Chrome for the full experience.

My signature keeps reappearing, or the mileage looks off


Your signature is shared, not per-template. Spot keeps one signature/footer per user across all your email templates, so editing it in one place changes it everywhere — that's why an old signature seems to "come back." Update it once in the Templates signature editor. See Email templates and signature.

Mileage and RPM are calculated from the board. The numbers in your Copy Load block and emails come from the load's origin, destination, and deadhead. If one looks wrong, re-check the pickup, delivery, and deadhead on the board.


Need help?

If none of the above sorts it, reach us directly:


Email: support@numeo.ai

WhatsApp: +1 206 569 4382

Telegram: t.me/numeo_support

In-app: the Help button in the side panel


Tell us your browser, the board you're on (DAT or Truckstop), and what you were doing — it helps us fix it faster.PreviousPlans and limitsNextCan't sign in

Emailing brokersBeginner
Email the broker from the load
Send a broker email in one click from the load — from your own mailbox, with your signature, and a review step before anything goes out.
3 min read

When a load looks good, you don't have to switch to your inbox and retype it. Numeo Spot lets you email the broker right from the load — from your own mailbox, with your signature attached, and a review step so you always see exactly what's about to send.

Send an email


Open a load on your DAT or Truckstop board.

Click to email the broker. Spot opens a compose widget with the load details already in front of you.

Pick a template if you have one, or type your message. Your signature is added automatically.

Review the confirm step, then send.


The email goes out from the mailbox you connected during sign-in — your own address, not a Numeo relay. Brokers reply straight to you.


Screenshot
Composing a broker email from a load in Numeo Spot
A product screenshot will be added here.

The review step

Before anything leaves your mailbox, Spot shows a confirm modal. What you see there is exactly what gets sent — the same to-address, subject, body, and signature. Nothing is sent in the background, and nothing is changed after you approve it. Read it, fix anything, then send.

Good to know


Templates and variables — save the emails you send over and over and fill them in per load. See Email templates and signature.

More than one mailbox — connect several and choose which one sends per search. See Send from multiple inboxes.

Daily allowance — the Free plan includes a daily number of broker emails. Pro removes the cap so you can send as many as your day needs. Compare on the pricing page.


Need a hand? Email support@numeo.ai or use the Help button in the side panel.PreviousConnect your mailbox to sendNextEmail templates and signature

Vetting brokers & loadsIntermediate
Factoring and credit checks
Connect your factoring company once and see each broker's credit and factoring status right on the load board.
4 min read

Numeo Spot shows each broker's factoring and credit status right on the load board, so you know who's likely to pay before you reach out. Connect your factoring company once, and the status rides along on the row — no separate tab, no re-checking each MC by hand.


Screenshot
Factoring status shown on a broker row in DAT
A product screenshot will be added here.

Connect your factoring company

You connect your provider by signing in to it the way you already do. Spot picks up that session and starts showing status on the board.


Open your factoring provider's site and log in as usual.

Spot captures the connection from that session — nothing to copy or paste.

Broker status starts appearing on the board for the loads you're looking at.


Providers Spot works with today: RTS, Triumph, WEX, PRO Funding (WinFactor), GSquared, Compass, TAFS, HaulPay, OTR Solutions, Engaged Financial, and ArtisPro.

Read the status

The letters depend on which provider you connected, since each factor uses its own labels. A couple of common patterns:


Triumph — A = Approved, D = Denied, N = No Buy, ? = Unknown.

Others — B = Buy, CF = Call First, NB = No Buy.


A No Buy is the one to slow down on: it means the factor won't buy that broker's invoices — often a fraud-risk flag, not just a slow payer. Treat it as "don't book without checking further."

What broker trust is built from

Spot doesn't have a separate "verify" button, and it isn't doing an FMCSA lookup for you. A broker's trustworthiness comes from two things you can see on the board:


Factoring and credit status — the letters above, straight from your connected factor.

DAT's own signals — whether the broker is a verified owner, how old their authority is, and the peer rating other carriers give that MC.


Put together, that's your read on a broker before you spend a call or an email on them. If the factoring status is clean and the DAT signals line up, you're in good shape. If a No Buy shows up, or the authority is brand new with no rating, that's your cue to dig before you book.

Next steps


Run the numbers with the profit calculator so the rate is worth the risk.

Once a broker checks out, email them in one click from the load.

Getting started
What is Load Hub?BeginnerLoad Hub runs one search across 15+ load boards and broker accounts, then dedupes and sorts them into a single table.
Sign in and set up your companyBeginnerSign in to Load Hub and complete the Company Information step — type your MC number and Numeo fills in your carrier details from FMCSA.
Install the Numeo Chrome extensionBeginnerInstall and sign in to the Numeo Chrome extension — it powers DAT and every broker-account source in Load Hub.
Connect your first sourceBeginnerTurn on at least one source so loads appear — some are on by default, others connect once. Meet the "Pick at least one source" nudge.

Connecting sources
Source types and the source barIntermediateThe source bar, the four kinds of source, and how to read the connected, expired, and not-connected pill states plus count badges.
Sources that need no setupBeginnerTruckStop Trial, Parade, HappyRobot, and Telegram work the moment you sign in — and three are pre-selected on every new search.
Connect broker accountsIntermediateConnect broker portal logins like Nolan, C.H. Robinson, TQL, and J.B. Hunt through the Numeo Chrome extension so their loads show in Load Hub.
Connect Sylectus and credential boardsIntermediateConnect Sylectus with its two-step corporate-then-user login. Plus where ITF and PLS stand in Load Hub today.
Search DAT loadsPower userTurn on DAT in Load Hub (Ultra plan + Numeo Chrome extension) — log in at one.dat.com, then search and DAT loads stream into your table.
Reconnect expired sourcesIntermediateRead the connected, expired, and not-connected source pills, and use the Reconnect dropdown to bring an expired broker or board back.

Searching loads
Run your first searchBeginnerSet an origin, destination, and equipment, then hit Search to pull matching loads from every source you've connected — in one board.
Work with search tabsIntermediateRun several lanes at once in tabs — each keeps its own filters, results, and pages, and a new tab pre-selects your connected sources.
Re-run a recent searchBeginnerYour last few days of searches are saved in the Recent Searches panel — re-run any lane in one click. History keeps four days.

Getting startedBeginner
Install the Numeo Spot Chrome extension
Add Numeo Spot from the Chrome Web Store, pin it to your toolbar, and open it on DAT or Truckstop in under a minute.
2 min read

Numeo Spot installs like any Chrome extension and is free. You'll be running it on your DAT or Truckstop board in about a minute.

Before you start


Use Google Chrome on a desktop or laptop (Spot is a Chrome extension).

Have your DAT or Truckstop login handy — that's where Spot's toolbar appears.


Install it


Open the Numeo Spot listing on the Chrome Web Store.

Click Add to Chrome, then Add extension to confirm.

Click the puzzle-piece icon in Chrome's toolbar and pin Numeo Spot so it's always one click away.



Screenshot
Pin Numeo Spot from the Chrome extensions menu
A product screenshot will be added here.

Open it on your board


Go to DAT (one.dat.com) or Truckstop and run a load search as usual.

Numeo Spot's toolbar appears on the board. Click the Numeo icon to open the side panel.

Sign in to start using it — see Sign in and connect your email.


Good to know


Spot auto-updates through Chrome — you'll always have the latest version, no manual reinstalls.

The extension only does its work on supported boards and portals; it doesn't change the rest of your browsing.
