AI Hub

AI Hub
The AI dispatcher that finds and ranks loads, negotiates by email, and prepares bookings — with your approval.Product overview


Get started
What is AI Hub?BeginnerAI Hub is the AI dispatcher that finds, ranks, negotiates, and prepares bookings — with your approval on every booking.
Meet the AI Hub agentsBeginnerThe AI Hub agents in plain English — search, scoring, chat, email, outreach, the send gate, and voice — who does what and how they hand off.
Connect your loadboards and emailBeginnerConnect the load-board sources AI Hub searches and a sending mailbox, plus the per-source city rules and how to reconnect.
Which sources search by state vs by cityIntermediatePer-source rules in AI Hub — DAT handles multi-state and zone searches; SPOT, RXO, Emerge, Mode, and Arrive each need a specific origin city.
Tabs and your first searchBeginnerCreate a search tab in AI Hub and run your first search — from the form or by just asking the chat.

Find & rank loads
Reading load statusesBeginnerThe load buckets in AI Hub — Open, Engaging, Ready to Book, Attention, Out, and Booked — and what each one means.
Load status referencePower userThe full map behind AI Hub's load buckets — which backend states roll into Open, Engaging, Ready to Book, Attention, Out, what shows a spinner, and the filter chips.
The search agentIntermediateHow AI Hub's search agent turns plain-English or form input into a structured load-board search — and where search ends and ranking begins.
How AI Hub ranks loadsIntermediateHow AI Hub scores and tiers loads — recommended, matched, potential — using RPM, deadhead, and live market context.
Market context on a load rowIntermediateReading the market data on an AI Hub load row — market RPM, the rate-range indicator, rate history, deadhead with tolls and a route map, and top reload destinations.

Ask Numeo AI
Ask Numeo AI (chat)BeginnerUse the AI Hub chat assistant to filter, rank, and answer questions about the loads on your board.
The planning agent behind the chatIntermediateWhat Ask Numeo AI does under the hood — the planning agent that breaks a request into steps and runs search and scoring tools, shown as it works.
Ask Numeo AI on the DAT boardIntermediateAsk Numeo AI on your DAT board — paint and rank loads, run the rate math, and start from a seed prompt.

Outreach & negotiate
How the broker-outreach agent worksIntermediateCold, multi-load broker outreach in AI Hub — how it triages a load dump, asks you which to chase, drafts replies, and counts each broker once.
How the email agent worksIntermediateThe single-load email agent runs one broker thread — it works out what a load still needs, asks for exactly that, and marks it Ready to Book.
How negotiation worksIntermediateThe negotiation approach in AI Hub — rate framed as a question, one position per email, ratecon rules, market anchoring, and you in control.
The emails inbox and broker threadsIntermediateWhere broker conversations live in AI Hub — the inline email rail, the needs-attention list, unread counts in the tab title, and how your replies steer the agent.

Automation modes
AI modes — Manual, Auto-Supervised, and Fully AutonomousIntermediateThe three AI Hub automation modes, what each one does, when the send gate kicks in, and how to switch — with semi-auto as the default.
Manual modeIntermediateManual mode keeps you at the keyboard — the agent finds and drafts, you compose and send, and nothing leaves without you. One exception is Book It.
Auto-Supervised mode (semi-auto)IntermediateThe default AI Hub mode — the agent drafts and auto-sends the safe stuff, while anything that commits or leans on remembered numbers comes back to you.
Fully Autonomous mode and personasPower userHow Fully Autonomous polls for loads, works them in batches, follows persona playbooks, and the safe-send guardrails that stop double-sends.
How mode rules are injectedPower userUnder the hood, each AI Hub agent gets mode-specific rules as a dispatcher-style message — not baked into its prompt — which is why the selector locks mid-run.

Booking & control
Book It and the booking flowIntermediateBook It sends your booking email instantly, pre-authorizes the load, and flips it to Booked only after the broker confirms.
Customize your Book It templatesIntermediateSet your first-touch and reply Book It templates, learn why rate placeholders stay blank, and manage your signature.
Booking HistoryBeginnerWhere confirmed bookings land in AI Hub — only after a broker confirms a Book It, with a little confetti and a booking-request timestamp that's never cleared.
Approvals and the human in the loopIntermediateWhen Numeo asks you to approve a broker draft, and how your answers, edits, and instructions steer the next reply.
How the send classifier worksPower userThe safety gate that judges every outbound draft in the automated modes — what it's fed, what it enforces, when it's in the path, and the post-Book-It exception.

Trust & safety
Trust, safety, factoring and blacklistPower userFactoring-grade and blacklist filters, MC dedupe, anti-loop guardrails, and prompt-injection safety on autonomous runs.
Factoring and broker credibilityPower userSet a factoring provider and minimum grade to filter which brokers reach your funnel — carried into autonomous runs, not a send-time block.
Blacklist and blocking brokersIntermediateBlock a broker to keep their loads out of your searches by MC — including on autonomous runs — and what blocking does and doesn't do.
Anti-double-send and loop safetyPower userHow AI Hub avoids double-emailing a broker or looping — MC-keyed dedupe, one send pipeline, an autonomous lease and action-log, and watchdogs.
Prompt-injection protectionPower userWhy a broker's email can't hijack the agent — broker messages are content only, and the only instructions the agent follows are yours.

Memory, voice & billing
Driver memory, voice and limitsPower userDriver long-term memory, spoken money-action confirmations on voice, and how Ask Numeo AI usage limits work.
Driver long-term memoryPower userHow AI Hub remembers driver preferences — advisory facts, an approval gate on broker-facing use, and why memory is off in Fully Autonomous.
Voice mode and confirmationsIntermediateVoice is a full mode of the same AI Dispatch conversation — money actions get a spoken read-back and a yes; search and questions run on their own.
Quotas and limitsIntermediateHow Ask Numeo AI usage is limited — a daily mobile message quota that resets at midnight Pacific, plus a per-plan web AI Hub search limit.

Troubleshooting & FAQ
Troubleshooting AI HubBeginnerFixes for the common snags — no connected source, reconnecting a mailbox, a Book It failed toast, and the mode selector locked mid-run.
AI Hub FAQBeginnerQuick answers to the recurring questions — does it auto-book, is there a Covered button, does it ever commit on its own, and when quotas reset.

Finding & booking loadsIntermediate
Check broker safety and report fraud
Read FMCSA, factoring, and fraud-risk signals on a load, and report a suspicious broker.
4 min read

Before you spend a call or an email on a load, Numeo helps you check who's behind it. The "Broker Info" tab on any load pulls together authority, payment, and fraud-risk signals so you can spot a bad actor before you book — not after.


Screenshot
The Broker Info tab showing FMCSA authority and fraud-risk flags
A product screenshot will be added here.

Read the Broker Info tab

Open a load and tap "Broker Info." You'll see the broker's basics and the checks that matter:


FMCSA authority — "FMCSA Authority Active" or "Inactive." Inactive is a reason to slow down.

DOT Number and MC Number — the broker's identifiers.

Email and Phone — how to reach them.

"Different Payment Address" — flagged when the remit-to address doesn't match, a common scam pattern.


Check factoring

Under "Factoring (Payment Verification Provider)" you can select your provider — Wex, RTS, Triumph, or Outgo — to see whether they'll buy that broker's invoices. A clean factoring status is one of the strongest "this broker pays" signals you have.

Read the fraud check

Numeo runs a "Fraud check" on the load and gives it a risk level: High, Medium, Low, or Unknown risk. Underneath, it lists the specific flags it found, in plain language — for example:


"FMCSA authority inactive"

"Public email domain (gmail, yahoo, …)"

"Newly registered email domain (< 1 year)"


You'll also get a short summary, like "Caution: this broker's MC authority is not active. Verify before booking." Treat a High-risk load as a stop sign: verify independently before you commit.

Report a suspicious load

If a load looks like a scam, flag it. On the load, tap "Report this load as fraud," add the required reason, and submit — you'll see "Report submitted." Your report is confidential and reviewed by the Numeo team, and it helps keep the board cleaner for every dispatcher.

Good to know


Signals, not a verdict. The fraud check surfaces risk so you can decide — you stay in control of whether to book.

Check before you commit. Make the Broker Info tab a habit before you book from the load details screen, especially on a rate that looks too good.

On the road (drivers)Beginner
The driver dashboard and your active trip
Your dashboard shows the active trip, ETA, Start Navigation, and an action center — everything you need for the load you're on.
3 min read

The driver dashboard is your home screen on the road. It shows the load you're on right now, your ETA, a one-tap Start Navigation, and a short list of the actions you reach for most.


Screenshot
The Numeo Driver dashboard with the active trip card
A product screenshot will be added here.

Your dashboard at a glance

When you open the app you'll see a greeting (Morning / Afternoon / Evening) and, below it, a few cards:


NUMEO INTELLIGENCE — short, road-aware tips, like "Optimal fuel stop ahead."

ACTIVE TRIP — the load you're running now, with its documents and Scheduled ETA.

ACTION CENTER — the quick actions for the current trip.


Active trip

The ACTIVE TRIP card is the load you're currently on. It carries the two documents that matter for the run — your BOL and POD — and your Scheduled ETA, so you can see whether you're on time.

Tap the card to open the full load. There you'll find Route Details, Dispatcher Notes, Hazmat Details, and the Financial & Route Summary (Total Rate and Your Payout). Under DOCUMENTS & PROOF, the load tells you what's needed and when: BOL required at pickup, POD required at delivery. See Scan and upload documents.

Start Navigation

Tap Start Navigation to hand the route to your phone's maps app for turn-by-turn directions. (If your phone can't open a maps app, you'll see "Maps app not available on this device.")

The in-app map is there to help you get your bearings and find what's close by. Open it for "Where to next?", see "You are here", and search Nearby Services — Fuel, Food, Rest, or Repair.

Action center

The ACTION CENTER keeps the common tasks one tap away:


Check-in — mark where you are on the trip.

Report Issue — flag a problem to your dispatcher.

Refer a Driver — share the app. ("Earn $250 for every verified driver who completes 10 loads.")


See all your trips

Beyond the current run, My Trips groups everything into three tabs — In Transit, Upcoming, and History — so you can look ahead to what's next or back at what you've delivered.

Good to know


This dashboard is the Numeo Driver side of the app. Dispatchers see a different home screen.

Turn-by-turn runs in your phone's maps app, not inside Numeo — so your usual navigation and voice guidance stay the same.

New offered loads don't appear here until you accept them and your dispatcher approves. See Accept a load from Opportunities.

Choose your sending inbox
Pick which connected inbox and company identity sends a broker email — it supplies the MC, DOT, signature, and template variables.
2 min read

If you send under more than one company or MC, every broker email needs to go out as the right identity. Load Hub lets you pick which connected inbox sends each message — and that choice fills in the rest of the email for you.

Pick the inbox on the load

When you compose an offer or book email from an expanded load, there's a selector for which connected inbox / company identity should send it. Choose the one that matches the authority you're booking under, and Load Hub sends from that inbox.


Screenshot
Choosing the sending inbox in the email composer
A product screenshot will be added here.

What the inbox supplies

Each connected inbox carries its own company details — MC, DOT, company name, and signature. Load Hub uses those to fill the email template automatically, so the broker sees the right identity every time without you retyping anything. Set your company details once during sign-in and onboarding and they ride along on the emails you send.

Connect your inboxes once and they're available on every load.

Good to know


Identity is per email, not per plan. Which inbox sends is your choice on each load — it isn't tied to your subscription.

Once it's sent, the reply comes back to the same place — see track broker replies.

Account, plans & billingBeginner
Manage your subscription
Upgrade, change, or cancel your plan through the secure Stripe checkout and Customer Portal.
3 min read

You manage your plan through a secure Stripe page on the web — upgrading, changing, and canceling all happen there. The app hands you off to it and picks up automatically once you're done. Here's how each step works.

Upgrade or change your plan


Go to your Profile and open Subscription / Manage Plan.

Choose the plan you want. The app opens a secure page on numeo.ai — you'll see the note "Plan changes are completed securely on numeo.ai".

Pay on the Stripe-hosted page with Apple Pay, Google Pay, or a card.

Your plan updates on its own once payment clears — no need to re-enter anything in the app.


If a payment doesn't go through, you'll see "Payment failed" — check your card details and try again.


Screenshot
Managing your plan from Profile in the Numeo App
A product screenshot will be added here.

Cancel or update your card

To cancel, swap your card, or grab an invoice, open the Stripe Customer Portal from your subscription settings. It's the same secure Stripe surface — you can downgrade, cancel, or update your payment method there, and your account reflects the change automatically.

Good to know


No app-store billing — Numeo doesn't charge through the App Store or Google Play. Everything runs through Stripe on the web.

Prices aren't shown in the app — see the pricing page for current costs, then complete the change on the secure Stripe page.

On Android you may be able to switch plans in place using your card on file; on iPhone the change happens on the web page.

Not sure what to pick? Compare limits and features in Plans and daily limits.

Troubleshooting & FAQBeginner
No results showing
No loads appear in Load Hub — pick at least one source, check your connections, widen the lane and Search Back, and read the empty-tab state.
3 min read

A search came back empty. Most of the time it's one of a few things — no source selected, a source that needs reconnecting, or a lane that's too tight. Here's the order to check.

Did you pick a source?

Load Hub only searches the sources you've selected. Search with none picked and you'll see a "Pick at least one source" nudge. Select at least one source in the source bar and search again. A few sources — TruckStop Trial, Parade, HappyRobot — are always available and three of them come pre-selected on a new tab, so you can search without connecting anything.

Is the tab actually searched?

An empty or never-searched tab shows the Recent Searches panel, not a results table. That's not an error — it just means this tab hasn't run yet. Set your filters and hit Search. See run your first search.

Are your sources connected?

If a source turned amber (expired), it won't return loads until you reconnect it. Scan the source bar for amber pills and reconnect them — see reconnect expired sources. After a search, Load Hub may also nudge you to "Connect more brokers" if you're searching a thin set of sources.

Is the lane too tight?

Filters can quietly filter everything out. Try loosening them:


Widen Origin / Destination, or drop deadhead caps (DH-O / DH-D).

Open up the Search Back window — set it to a longer window or All so you're not limited to the last hour. See the Search Back window.

Relax rate and mileage filters (RPM, Min Rate, Min/Max Mi).


Good to know


Empty but no upgrade prompt? That's a source or filter issue, not a limit. If you do see an upgrade prompt, you've hit your search quota.

DAT showing nothing is usually its own setup — see DAT not working.

Getting startedBeginner
Download Numeo and sign in
Install Numeo AI Dispatch from the App Store and sign in with an email code, Google, or Apple.
3 min read

The Numeo app puts dispatch in your pocket — search, bid, and book loads from your phone. This page gets you from a fresh install to signed in, in a couple of minutes.


Screenshot
The Numeo app splash screen with Get Started and Sign In
A product screenshot will be added here.

Install the app

On iPhone, search the App Store for "Numeo AI Dispatch"; on Android, find Numeo on Google Play. Install it, and when you open it for the first time you'll see the welcome screen — "Find loads. Book faster." with the line "Search, bid, and book — from your phone."


New here? Tap "Get Started".

Already have an account? Tap "Sign In".


Sign in with an email code

The simplest way in is your email. No password to remember.


On "Sign in or create an account", enter your email — the screen reads "Enter your email to sign in or create an account."

Tap through to "Verify email". We send a one-time code to that inbox.

On "Enter code", type the code from the email. That's it — you're in.


The same flow signs you in and creates your account, so it works whether or not you've used Numeo before.

Or continue with Google or Apple

Under "or continue with", you can tap "Sign in with Google" or "Sign in with Apple" instead. Pick the account you use for work and you're signed in — no code needed.

Have an invite code?

If a friend or dispatcher shared a Numeo invite, tap "Have an invite code?" on the sign-in screen and enter it. Joining through an invite gives both of you extra daily load searches — see Invite friends and earn searches for how the rewards work.

Next steps

Once you're in, Numeo walks you through a short setup so brokers can reach you and your loads are relevant:

Working with resultsIntermediate
Hide duplicate loads
How Load Hub spots the same freight across boards, the hide-duplicates toggle, per-source duplicate counts, and server-side dedup.
3 min read

The same freight often posts on several boards at once. Load Hub spots those copies and can collapse them into one row, so you scan real loads instead of the same one three times.

Turn on hide duplicates

Flip the hide duplicates toggle and Load Hub folds each set of copies into a single row. Turn it off to see every posting from every source, copies included.

How Load Hub knows it's a duplicate

Two postings are treated as the same load when these line up:


pickup city and state

delivery city and state

rate

miles

equipment


When all five match across sources, it's the same freight wearing different board logos — so Load Hub keeps one and hides the rest.

Per-source duplicate counts

Even with duplicates hidden, each source still shows how many copies it contributed, alongside its total count. That tells you which boards are echoing the same freight versus which are bringing loads you wouldn't have seen otherwise.

Two layers of dedup

Load Hub deduplicates in two places:


On the server — the unified search collapses obvious repeats before results ever reach you.

In your table — the hide-duplicates toggle gives you the final say on the rows you're looking at.


Good to know


Hiding duplicates works alongside sorting and column order and the Hide Selected button — set them together for a clean board. See sort, reorder, and hide duplicates.

For what each column means, see reading the results table.

Work with search tabs
Run several lanes at once in tabs — each keeps its own filters, results, and pages, and a new tab pre-selects your connected sources.
3 min read

Load Hub is tabbed, so you can keep more than one lane going side by side instead of retyping a search every time you switch. Each tab is its own search — its own filters, results, and pages.

Add a tab

Click "+" to open a new search tab. It pre-selects the sources you've already connected, so you're ready to search without picking sources again.

A fresh tab opens on "Anywhere" for both origin and destination until you set them. Fill in the lane and hit Search — see Run your first search.


Screenshot
Several Load Hub search tabs open at once

Each tab is independent

Switching tabs doesn't disturb the others:


Every tab holds its own filters — origin, destination, equipment, and the rest.

Troubleshooting & FAQIntermediate
A source expired or won't connect
A broker or board turned amber or won't connect — reconnect from the dropdown, re-authenticate the extension, or re-run the login.
3 min read

Broker and board logins time out — it's normal. When a source turns amber or won't connect, the fix is usually a quick reconnect. Here's how to read the state and get it back.

Read the pill

Every source in the source bar is a pill in one of three states:


Connected — a blue checkbox. Working.

Expired — an amber warning. It was connected, but the login timed out.

Not connected — a plus-circle. Never set up.


The header keeps a count of "{n} disconnected broker(s)" when some have dropped. See reconnect expired sources for the full rundown.

Reconnect an expired source


When you have disconnected brokers, a "Reconnect" dropdown appears in the source bar, listing each one with how long ago it dropped — "expired Xh/Xd ago".

Pick the source to reconnect it. It returns to a blue check and its loads flow back in.


If it still won't connect


Broker accounts connect through the Numeo Chrome extension. If a reconnect fails, make sure the extension is installed and signed in, then try the broker connect flow again.

Sylectus reconnects through its own login window — re-enter the corporate then user credentials. See connect Sylectus and credential boards.

DAT has its own requirements — see DAT not working.


Good to know


Hover any pill to see its action — the tooltip reads Enable, Disable, Connect, or Reconnect.

If a lane looks light, scan the source bar first: an amber pill returns no loads until you reconnect it.

Get startedBeginner
Connect your loadboards and email
Connect the load-board sources AI Hub searches and a sending mailbox, plus the per-source city rules and how to reconnect.
3 min read

Before AI Hub can search or send, it needs two things connected: at least one load-board source to search, and a mailbox to send broker email from. Here's how each one works and what to do when a connection drops.

Connect a source

Sources are the boards AI Hub searches. DAT is selected by default, and you need at least one connected source on a search. If nothing is selected, the board tells you:


Select at least one connected source to search.


Pick your sources per tab, then run the search.

Per-source city and state rules

Not every source can do a broad search. This is enforced as you build the search, so it's worth knowing up front:


Only DAT supports multi-state and zone searches. If you search by state or zone, DAT is the source that returns results.

Other sources need a specific origin city. These require a city and return nothing on a state-only search: SPOT, RXO, Emerge, Mode, and Arrive.


Hover a disabled source and you'll see why:


Only DAT supports multi-state / zone searches. Enter a specific city to include this source.



This source requires a specific origin city — state-only searches return no results.


The short version: searching a whole state or zone? That's DAT. Add a specific origin city to bring the other sources in.

Connect a sending mailbox

Working a broker thread — and sending the Book It email — needs a connected mailbox. Each tab sends from its own sender email, so the outreach and booking emails on that tab go out from the address you set for it.

Reconnect a source or mailbox

Connection health shows in a status banner and badge on the search sources. If a source or mailbox stops working, you'll see it flagged there — reconnect it from the banner and you're back in business.

Automation modesPower user
Fully Autonomous mode and personas
How Fully Autonomous polls for loads, works them in batches, follows persona playbooks, and the safe-send guardrails that stop double-sends.
5 min read

Fully Autonomous is the hands-off mode: the agent watches your search, works loads in batches, and drafts and sends under the send gate without checking in on every step. It's built for volume. This article covers what "autonomous" actually does — the polling, the batch behavior, persona playbooks, and the guardrails that keep it from double-sending or running away — and where the human stays firmly in the loop.

If you're deciding between modes first, start with AI modes.

How an autonomous run behaves

Instead of running once when you search, Fully Autonomous keeps a watcher on the tab and wakes up to work new matches as they appear. You'll see autonomous runs surfaced in the UI with poll controls and a run card, so you can watch what it's doing and stop it when you want.


Screenshot
An autonomous run in progress with poll controls
A product screenshot will be added here.

By default the agent works a fixed batch — roughly 10 to 20 loads at a time — rather than trying to email everything at once. That keeps volume predictable and your outbox sane. The batch behavior changes when a persona is active (below).

Persona playbooks

A persona is an advanced capability Numeo can turn on for your account — a playbook tuned to your operation and truck type. It's selected internally by equipment type behind a feature flag, not something you author, create, or add yourself. When a persona is active, the agent follows the playbook instead of the default batch behavior.

A persona shapes the same four things the defaults handle:


Without a persona: the fixed 10–20 load batch, default ranking, default negotiation rules.

With a persona: load selection, ranking, volume, and negotiation all follow the playbook.


Because a persona is tuned to a specific operation, it's a path Numeo enables for you rather than a setting you toggle. If a persona would fit how you run, ask us to turn one on for your account.

The safe-send guardrails

Autonomous mode does more on its own, so it leans on several guardrails that keep it safe. You don't configure these — they're always on — but it helps to know they're there:


One broker, counted once. Outreach is deduped by broker MC number, so a re-run or restart won't cold-email the same broker again. This is the same mechanism behind the "already contacted" tooltip.

A lease and an action log. Autonomous side-effects are recorded, so a re-triggered search or a service restart can't re-send an email that already went out.

Anti-loop protection. Built-in run gating, active-run tracking, a circuit breaker, and a loop detector stop the agent from spinning or repeating itself.

Send acknowledgement recovery. If a send drops mid-flight, a watchdog recovers it rather than silently firing twice.

Pause means pause. You can stop the agent, and it stops picking up new work.


Together these are why "autonomous" doesn't mean "unsupervised risk" — the failure modes that would matter most (double-sends, loops, re-sends after a restart) are guarded against by design.

What autonomous still won't do

This is the important part. Fully Autonomous automates the outreach and negotiation drafting — it does not remove you from the commitment:


Booking a load is still your call. The agent never sends a booking commitment on its own; that's always Book It, your explicit pre-authorization.

Driver long-term memory is off in this mode for the send gate — the agent won't lean on remembered numbers to make broker-facing claims.

Voice money-actions require a spoken "yes." Booking, bidding, or sending anything to a broker over voice always gets a read-back and an explicit confirmation.


So even at full automation, the money decisions stay with you. The agent handles the volume of typing and chasing; you keep the commit.

Working the load & AIIntermediate
Call the broker from the load board
Dial the broker straight from a load using your phone, Google Voice, RingCentral, or Zoom — no copying numbers into another app.
3 min read

When you're ready to talk numbers, you can call the broker right from the load — no digging the number out of the posting and pasting it into another app. Numeo Spot gives you a few ways to dial, so you can use whatever phone setup you already have.

Your calling options

On a load, Spot lets you place the call through any of these:


Call — a plain phone dial (tel:). Opens the load's number in whatever your computer uses to make calls.

Google Voice — dials through your Google Voice line.

Ring Central Web — click-to-dial through RingCentral in your browser. This is the deep integration (see below).

Zoom — places the call through Zoom.


Pick the one that matches how you already make calls. Nothing to copy, nothing to retype.

Connect RingCentral for click-to-dial

RingCentral is the one that hooks in most closely. Once it's connected, you can click a broker's number and RingCentral places the call in your browser — no separate app, no dialing by hand.

To connect it:


Open the Numeo Spot popup from the toolbar icon.

Go to the VoIP tab.

Sign in to RingCentral to link your account.


After that, the Ring Central Web option dials for you whenever you're working a load. Spot will show you when the connection is live, and flag it if the call is blocked or the link drops.


Screenshot
The VoIP tab in the Numeo Spot popup
A product screenshot will be added here.

Before you call

A quick check before you dial saves a wasted call:


Look at the factoring and credit status on the row so you already know how the broker sits.

Have the profit, RPM, and deadhead in front of you so you can talk rate with real numbers.

Prefer to reach out in writing first? Email the broker in one click and call as the follow-up.

Load details & profitabilityIntermediate
Load details and profitability
Expand a load for the four-panel detail — equipment, route and tolls, broker, and email — plus the profitability calculator and broker status.
4 min read

Click any row and it opens into the full load detail — everything you need to decide on one screen, without leaving the table. In Load Hub the detail is laid out in four panels: Equipment, Trip & Map, Broker, and Email.


Screenshot
A load expanded into the four-panel detail view
A product screenshot will be added here.

The four panels


Equipment — the equipment type and specifics for the load.

Trip & Map — the route, the trip schedule, and a map. You can turn on toll routing to see the route with tolls factored in.

Broker — who's posting: company, contact, and the broker's status (see below).

Email — compose and track your outreach right here. See Email a broker and book.


Route, map, and tolls

The Trip & Map panel plots origin to destination and lays out the pickup and delivery schedule. Toll route controls let you switch tolls on so the mileage and route reflect what the trip actually costs to run — which feeds straight into the profit math.

The profitability calculator

The profitability calculator turns the load's rate and miles into real numbers so you're not doing lane math in your head. It breaks down the costs and shows what's left. It assumes 7 MPG by default — adjust it to your truck and the estimate updates.

Use it to sanity-check RPM before you reach out: a good rate on a long deadhead with tolls can look very different once the costs are in.

Mark the broker: Favorite or Blacklist

Every broker in the detail has a status control. You can mark a broker a Favorite so their loads stand out next time, or Blacklist one to flag on their loads, and Remove the mark to clear it. It's a fast way to teach the board which brokers you actually want to work with.

Good to know


Where the data comes from varies by source, so some loads show richer detail than others — connected brokers and boards can carry extra fields like comments or source-specific info.

The email panel is the handoff. Once the numbers work, move straight into the offer email without copying anything across — Email a broker and book.

Finding & booking loadsIntermediate
Verify a broker with Broker Info
Read FMCSA authority, DOT/MC, payment address, and factoring status on the Broker Info tab.
3 min read

Before you spend a call or an email on a load, check who's behind it. The "Broker Info" tab on any load gathers the broker's authority, identifiers, payment details, and factoring status in one place — so you can vet them in a few seconds.


Screenshot
The Broker Info tab with FMCSA authority and factoring
A product screenshot will be added here.

Open the Broker Info tab

Tap a load, then tap "Broker Info." You'll see the broker's basics and the checks that matter:


FMCSA authority — "FMCSA Authority Active" or "Inactive." Inactive is a reason to slow down and verify before you book.

DOT Number and MC Number — the broker's identifiers, ready to copy or look up.

Email and Phone — how to reach them.

"Different Payment Address" — flagged when the remit-to address doesn't match the broker on file. That mismatch is a common scam pattern, so treat it as a caution.


Check factoring

Under "Factoring (Payment Verification Provider)", pick your provider — Wex, RTS, Triumph, or Outgo — to run a factoring check. A clean result means your factor is comfortable buying that broker's invoices, a strong "this broker actually pays" signal.

Good to know


Signals, not a verdict — Broker Info shows what's true about the broker; you decide whether to book.

Fraud risk and reporting live on this same tab. For the risk levels and how to flag a scam, see Check broker safety and report fraud — the article that owns the fraud workflow.

Getting startedBeginner
Complete onboarding and your profile
Set your role, MC/DOT, and equipment in the short setup wizard, then find your first load.
4 min read

Right after you sign in, Numeo runs a short setup wizard. It takes a minute and does two things: tells brokers who they're dealing with, and tunes the load board to your equipment and lanes. Do it once and everything after is faster.


Video walkthrough
Walkthrough: complete onboarding and find your first load
📹 We can record this walkthrough for you — just ask the Numeo team.

Walk through the setup

The wizard moves through a few quick screens. Answer each and tap forward.


Contact — "Let's get to know you." Enter your name and your MC / DOT Number. Brokers use this to look you up, so it's worth getting right.

Role — "What is your role?" Pick the one that fits: Driver, Dispatcher, Company Owner, Operations Manager, or Dispatch Service Provider.

Employment — "What type of driver are you?" Choose Company Driver or Owner Operator.

Equipment — "Select your equipment." Pick what you haul. This is what drives your recommended loads.

Find your first load — "Let's find your next load." Tap "Find My First Load" and Numeo runs your first search.


Why the MC/DOT matters

Numeo asks for your MC or DOT so brokers can respond to you. Before you can bid on or email a broker, you'll need your phone and MC/DOT on file. If they're missing, you'll see a prompt: "Add your phone & MC/DOT to search loads" — with the reason underneath, "Brokers need these to respond to your bids."

If you skipped a field during setup, add it later from your profile — no need to start over.

Good to know


Change any answer anytime. Your role, equipment, and company details all live in your profile, so you can update them as your operation changes.

Better answers, better loads. The "Recommended" sort on the board is built from what you enter here. A complete profile means fewer irrelevant rows.

Outreach & negotiateIntermediate
How negotiation works
The negotiation approach in AI Hub — rate framed as a question, one position per email, ratecon rules, market anchoring, and you in control.
4 min read

When AI Hub works a rate with a broker, it follows a deliberately careful style: it asks for a number instead of asserting one, keeps each email to a single ask, and never touches a rate confirmation unless you've told it to. The point isn't to hand off your negotiation — it's to do the back-and-forth typing while you keep every decision.

The approach in four rules

These are the guardrails the agent negotiates under. They're worth knowing because they shape every draft you'll approve.


Rate as a question, not a claim. The agent writes "can you do $2,850 all-in?" — never "the rate is $2,850." A question keeps the door open and keeps you from being pinned to a number you didn't authorize.

One position per email. It won't bundle a rate ask, a pickup change, and a question about a ratecon into one message. One clear ask per email keeps the thread readable and the broker's answer unambiguous.

No ratecon until you say so. A rate confirmation is a hard line — once it lands, you're locked into accept-or-walk. So the agent will not ask for one unless you explicitly tell it to.

Never fabricate. If a detail isn't known, the agent asks for it rather than inventing it. Same goes for numbers grounded in driver memory — those route through your approval before they can be said to a broker.


Market anchoring

The agent doesn't negotiate blind. It can pull market context for the lane — the current market rate, the RPM range, and recent rate history — the same figures you see on a load row. That gives its ask a reference point instead of a guess.


Screenshot
Market rate and rate history on a load row
A product screenshot will be added here.

Anchoring cuts both ways: it keeps the agent from lowballing a hot lane and from chasing a rate the market won't bear. You can always override the number — the market read is context for your decision, not a rule the agent follows on its own.

Where your approval sits

Every reply the agent wants to send passes through a send classifier before it goes out — the gate that decides whether a draft is safe to auto-send or needs your sign-off. How strict that gate is depends on your AI mode:


In Manual, you compose and send — nothing leaves without you.

In Auto-Supervised and Fully Autonomous, drafts run through the classifier, and anything that makes a commitment or leans on remembered numbers comes back to you first.


No mode lets the agent commit money on its own. That's what Book It is for — your explicit go-ahead to send a booking email.

When the broker says yes

The agent watches for acceptance in the broker's reply. Phrases like "deal," "book it," "sending rate con," or "you got it" are read as a hard yes. At that point the load moves toward booking — but a booking only becomes final after the broker confirms against your Book It, not the moment the agent detects a "yes." You're never committed by the agent's reading of a message alone.

FiltersIntermediate
Every search filter, explained
A field-by-field guide to Load Hub's filters — deadhead, pickup, load type, size, RPM, min rate, mileage, and how far back to look.
4 min read

Load Hub gives you two rows of filters: a main row to set the lane, and a second row to tighten the results by pay, distance, and freshness. Here's what every field does.


Screenshot
Load Hub's main and secondary filter rows
A product screenshot will be added here.

Main filter row

This is the lane itself — where the load runs and what you're hauling.


Origin — pickup city and state ("Origin city, state"). Next to it, DH-O sets your deadhead-to-origin limit: the furthest you'll drive empty to reach the pickup.

Destination — drop city and state ("Destination city, state"), with DH-D for deadhead on the destination end.

Equipment — your trailer type and any subtypes.

Pickup — a date range for when the load picks up.

Load Type — Full or Partial.

Max Length / Weight — cap the load to what you can haul, set in Length (ft) and Weight (lbs).

Search — run it.


More filters

The second row trims the results down to loads worth your time.


Sources — pick which boards and brokers to include; the chip shows "{n} sources".

RPM ($/mi) — minimum rate per mile.

Min Rate ($) — minimum total rate.

Min Mi / Max Mi — shortest and longest trip you'll take.

Search Back — how far back to pull postings: All, 1 hour, 3 hours, 6 hours, 12 hours, 24 hours, or 48 hours. A tighter window keeps the board to fresh loads.


Apply, Reset, and Hide Selected


Apply / Reset — one toggle: apply your filter changes, or clear them back to defaults.

Hide Selected — once you've checked some rows, this appears and hides them, so you can clear out loads you've already worked or ruled out.


Good to know


To search more than one origin or destination together, see multi-location and zones.

Deadhead (DH-O / DH-D), rate, RPM, and age are also sortable columns in the results table — see reading the results table.

Troubleshooting & FAQBeginner
FMCSA company lookup issues
The MC lookup can't find your company during onboarding — check the MC number or enter your DOT, company, and address by hand.
2 min read

During onboarding, Load Hub looks up your company from your MC number so you don't have to type your carrier details. If the lookup can't find you, you can still finish — just fill the fields in yourself.

How the lookup should work

On the "Company Information" step, you type your "MC Number" and Load Hub runs a live FMCSA lookup — you'll see "Searching FMCSA…" and matching carriers listed as "MC {number} · DOT {number} · City, ST". Pick yours and it fills in "Company Name", "DOT Number", "Phone", and "Address". See sign in and set up your company.

If it can't find your company


Double-check the MC number. A wrong digit is the most common cause. Re-type it and let the lookup run again.

Give it a moment. The lookup pulls live from FMCSA — if it's slow, pause before retyping.

Enter the details by hand. If your carrier still doesn't appear, fill in Company Name, DOT Number, Phone, and Address yourself, then continue. New authorities can take time to show in FMCSA's records, so manual entry is the right move if you're recently registered.


Good to know


The company identity you set here rides along on the broker emails you send from Load Hub, so it's worth getting the MC and DOT right — you can edit the fields before saving.

Every broker email you send lives in Conversations, threaded per load. That's where you send bids, fire back counter offers, and pull a dispatcher onto the deal when you want a second set of hands — all in one place, without digging through your inbox.

Where your threads live

Open "Conversations" to see each broker exchange grouped by load. Reply or forward right from the thread, so the whole back-and-forth on a deal stays together instead of scattered across your mailbox.

If you've connected more than one mailbox, use the "All inboxes" switcher to see everything at once or focus on a single address.


Screenshot
Broker conversations threaded per load in the Numeo App
A product screenshot will be added here.

Send a bid or ask for info

Bids, info requests, and counter offers all happen inside the thread — see Send bids and counter offers.

Invite a dispatcher onto the thread

Want a dispatcher on the deal? Tap "Invite Dispatcher" to CC them onto the thread. They see the full conversation and can jump in — useful when you're driving and want someone else closing the paperwork, or when a teammate is covering your board.

Use templates to send faster

Reusable email templates with variables and your signature live in Customize email templates.

Good to know


Your address, not a relay — threads send from the Gmail or Outlook mailbox you connected (OAuth 2.0, no third-party relay). Brokers reply straight to you.

Let AI draft it — you can also hand the outreach to Ask Numeo AI to find and book, which drafts the broker email for you and checks the broker before it goes out.

New to mailboxes? Start with Set up your mailbox and email brokers.

Account, plans & billingPower user
Request a managed dispatch plan
Hand your loads to real human dispatchers, 24/7, with the Dispatch Plan — and request a callback to get started.
2 min read

Some weeks you don't want to work the boards at all — you just want loads booked. The Dispatch Plan is Numeo's managed dispatch service: real people handle your dispatching for you, around the clock. It's separate from the app's search and AI tools, and it's optional.

What the Dispatch Plan is

With the Dispatch Plan, real human dispatchers work your loads for you, 24/7 — finding freight, talking to brokers, and booking on your behalf. Pricing starts "From 1.5%" of the load, so what you pay tracks what you actually book. Current terms are on the pricing page.

This is a hands-off option for when you'd rather have a team run your dispatch than do it yourself. You can keep using the app's own search and AI Dispatch tools alongside it.

Request a callback

To get started, use "Request a callback" from the Dispatch Plan screen in the app. Someone from the dispatch team reaches out to walk you through how it works and set things up for your operation.

Good to know


It's a service, not just a plan switch — unlike upgrading your subscription, the Dispatch Plan pairs you with human dispatchers, so it starts with a conversation.

Need help on a single load instead? If you just want a person to step in on one deal, you can pull in a human from the AI chat — see Get human dispatcher support.

Send from multiple inboxes
Connect more than one mailbox and choose which address sends per DAT search — a primary sender, per-search overrides, and CC.
3 min read

If you work more than one mailbox — a personal address, a company address, a lane-specific one — Numeo Spot lets you connect them all and pick which one sends. You choose per DAT search, so the right address goes out on the right loads.

Connect another mailbox

You connected your first mailbox when you signed in. To add more, connect each one the same way — with send access — from the toolbar's Connect Email. Spot supports several mailboxes on one account.

Pick the sender per search

Use the Search Email selector on the on-board toolbar to choose which mailbox sends for the DAT search you're working.


Primary email — your default sender across searches.

Per-search override — switch the sender for the current DAT search without changing your default. The next search can use a different one.


This keeps company loads going out from the company address and everything else from wherever it belongs — without you having to remember to switch inboxes.


Screenshot
The Search Email selector on the Numeo Spot toolbar
A product screenshot will be added here.

CC

You can CC another address on broker emails — loop in a partner, a second desk, or your own records without a separate send.

Good to know


The sender you pick applies to emails you send from that search, including from your templates.

Every send still goes through the review step — you'll see the from-address before it goes out.

Finding & booking loadsBeginner
Book or contact a broker from a load
Act right from a load — Slide to Book, call or email the broker, ask for info, save, or share.
3 min read

When a load looks right, you don't switch apps to act on it. Every action you need sits on the load's detail screen — book it, call or email the broker, ask a quick question, or hold it for later.


Screenshot
The action row on a load detail screen
A product screenshot will be added here.

Slide to Book

The fastest path is Slide to Book. Drag the slider across and Numeo books the load — you'll see it confirm with "Booked!" or "Booking confirmed." The slide gesture is deliberate, so you don't book by an accidental tap.

Reach the broker

Not ready to book? Reach out first:


Call Broker — dial the broker straight from the load.

Email Broker — open a message to the broker. (Emailing needs a connected mailbox — see Set up your mailbox and email brokers.)

Ask info — send a quick question about the load.

Get price — ask the broker for the rate.


Hold or pass it along


Save load — bookmark it to your Saved Loads to come back to (see Sort and save loads).

Share Load — send the load to someone else.

Get directions — hand the route to your phone's maps app.


Before you book

Give the broker a look first. The "Broker Info" tab shows FMCSA authority, factoring, and fraud-risk flags — a quick check that saves you from a bad booking. Walk through it in Verify a broker with Broker Info and Check broker safety and report fraud.

To bid or email a broker, your phone and MC/DOT need to be on file — see Add your phone and MC/DOT.

On the road (drivers)Beginner
Driver navigation and nearby services
Use the in-app map to get your bearings and find fuel, food, rest, or repair — turn-by-turn hands off to your phone's maps app.
3 min read

The app's map helps you see where you're headed and find what's close by. When it's time for turn-by-turn, Numeo hands the route to your phone's maps app — the one you already use — so your usual directions and voice guidance stay the same.


Screenshot
The in-app driver map with Nearby Services
A product screenshot will be added here.

Start navigation

Tap Start Navigation from your dashboard or your active trip. Numeo opens the route in your phone's maps app for turn-by-turn directions.

Numeo doesn't run turn-by-turn itself — it passes the route to Apple Maps, Google Maps, or whatever your phone uses. If your phone can't open a maps app, you'll see "Maps app not available on this device" or "Unable to open maps application"; open your maps app manually in that case.

The in-app map

Open the map inside Numeo to orient yourself before or during a run:


"Where to next?" — a quick read on your next stop.

"You are here" — your current position on the map.


This map is for getting your bearings and finding what's nearby, not for turn-by-turn — that's what Start Navigation is for.

Find nearby services

Tap "Nearby Services" to search for what's around you right now:


Fuel

Food

Rest

Repair


Pick a category and the map shows the closest options, so you can plan a stop without leaving the app.

Good to know


Turn-by-turn lives in your phone's maps app, not inside Numeo — your saved routes, traffic, and voice prompts work exactly as they always do.

The map's Fuel search finds stops near you. For logging what you spent, see Track fuel receipts and statements.

Your active trip, ETA, and the Start Navigation button all live on the driver dashboard.

Reset your password
Recover access to Load Hub with the forgot-password and set-password flow on the sign-in page.
2 min read

Locked out of Load Hub? You can reset your password from the sign-in page — no need to contact support to get back in.

Reset from the sign-in page


Open the Load Hub sign-in page.

Choose the forgot password option.

Enter the email on your Numeo account. Load Hub sends you a reset link.

Follow the link and set a new password, then sign back in.


Because it's the same Numeo account you use across Numeo Spot and the app, the new password works everywhere you sign in with that email.

If you signed in with Google or Microsoft (OAuth), there's no Numeo password to reset — use that provider's Continue with Google or Continue with Microsoft button on the sign-in page instead.

Good to know


Use the account email. The reset goes to the email tied to your Numeo account — the one you signed up with.

Resetting your password doesn't touch your connected sources or company details — you land back where you left off.

Read the load details
Route map, stops, market rate, the Tolls and Fuel calculator, and booking with Slide to Book.
5 min read

Tapping a load opens its full detail screen — everything you need to size up the run and act on it, without leaving the app. It's split into two tabs: "Load Info" for the freight and the route, and "Broker Info" for who's behind it.


Screenshot
The load details screen with the Load Info and Broker Info tabs
A product screenshot will be added here.

Route and stops

Under "Route Details" you'll see each stop — pickup and delivery — with its city, state, and date. Tap "Show in Map" to see the lane on a map, and "Get directions" to hand the route to your phone's maps app.

Load info

The Load Info tab lays out the freight:


Commodity, Equipment, and Distance

Length, Weight, and Full or Partial

Hazmat and Team flags

Requirements — or "None specified by broker" if the broker didn't list any

Notes from the broker


Market rate

Numeo tells you how the offered rate stacks up against the lane. Look for the market read — for example "${diff}/mi above market" — plus the Lowest, Medium, and Highest RPM for that lane. It's a quick gut-check on whether the rate is worth a call.

Tolls and Fuel calculator

Tap "Get Tolls" to run the "Tolls & Fuel" calculator and see the toll and fuel cost for that specific load — real money that comes off your rate. On the free plan you get a set number of checks per lane; you'll see "Tolls & Fuel ({count} free)" and, once they're used, "Free Toll Checks Used" with an "Unlock Toll Routes" prompt. A paid plan lets you "Compare up to 4 toll routes per lane" and "See exact toll costs for each route." See pricing for what's included.

Book or contact the broker

When the load looks good, act right from the details screen:


Slide to Book — drag the slider to book; it confirms with "Booked!" / "Booking confirmed."

Call Broker or Email Broker — reach out directly.

Ask info / Get price — send a quick question or ask for the rate.

Save load — bookmark it for later (see Sort and save loads).

Share Load — send it to someone else.


Before you book

Flip to the Broker Info tab and give the broker a look first — FMCSA authority, factoring status, and fraud-risk flags all live there. Walk through it in Check broker safety and report fraud.

Troubleshooting & FAQBeginner
Load Hub FAQ
Quick answers — recent-search retention, whether booking is in-app, duplicates, TruckStop Trial vs Account, and multi-MC.
3 min read

Short answers to the questions that come up most. For anything deeper, follow the links.

How long are my recent searches kept?

Recent searches are saved on the server for 4 days, split into Today and Past Week. Re-run any of them with one click. See recent searches.

Does "Book It" book the load in the app?

No. The book email is an email offer to the broker, sent from the composer in the load's Email panel. It's not an in-app booking or dispatch confirmation — there's no button that reserves the load on the broker's system. You send your offer; the broker confirms on their side. See email a broker and book.

Why do I see the same load more than once?

The same load can post on more than one board, so it shows up more than once. Turn on the hide-duplicates toggle to collapse them, and Load Hub also dedups on the server side. See hide duplicate loads.

What's the difference between TruckStop Trial and TruckStop Account?

TruckStop Trial is an always-available source — no connection needed, and it's pre-selected on a new tab. TruckStop Account is your own connected TruckStop login, added through the broker connect flow so results come from your account.

Can I run more than one MC?

On the web, Load Hub gives you two things rather than a single MC switcher:


Sending identity per email — choose which inbox / company identity sends each broker email, each carrying its own MC and DOT.

A company filter — show or hide loads by broker/company name to focus the table.


A full multi-MC company switcher isn't part of the web Load Hub today.

Good to know


Still stuck on empty results or a dropped source? See no results showing and a source expired or won't connect.

Searching loadsBeginner
Run your first search
Set an origin, destination, and equipment, then hit Search to pull matching loads from every source you've connected — in one board.
3 min read

Load Hub searches all your connected load boards and broker accounts at once. Tell it where the load picks up, where it drops, and what you're hauling, then hit Search — matching loads land in one table you can sort and work.

Before you start


You need at least one source selected. A new search tab comes with TruckStop Trial, Parade, and HappyRobot already picked — these are always on, no connecting required. To pull from brokers like TQL, C.H. Robinson, or DAT, connect those sources first.

If you search with nothing selected, Load Hub nudges you to "Pick at least one source."


Run a search


Open Load Hub at /dispatcher/load-hub.

In Origin, type where the load picks up — "Origin city, state".

In Destination, type where it drops — "Destination city, state". Leave either end blank to search open on that side.

Set Equipment — your trailer type and any subtypes.

Click Search.


Results fill the table. From there you can sort them, expand a load for the full detail, and email the broker.


Screenshot
The Load Hub search bar with Origin, Destination, and Equipment set
A product screenshot will be added here.

Work several searches at once

Load Hub is tabbed, so you can keep more than one lane going side by side. Each tab holds its own filters, results, and pages.


Click "+" to add a tab. It pre-selects the sources you've already connected, so you're ready to search right away.

A fresh tab opens on "Anywhere" for origin and destination until you set them.

An empty tab — one you haven't searched yet — shows your Recent Searches in place of an empty table, so you can jump back into a lane in one click.


Good to know


Narrow the results with search filters — rate, RPM, deadhead, pickup date, and more.

Search more than one origin or destination at once with multi-location search.

Keep a hot lane current with Auto Refresh.

Notifications and community
Turn on push and radar alerts, choose where they land, and join other dispatchers in the Numeo community on Telegram.
3 min read

Numeo can notify you when a matching load posts. Turn on notifications to get your radar alerts, pick where they land, and join other dispatchers in the Numeo community on Telegram.

Manage your notifications

Your notifications live in one hub with All, Unread, and Invitations tabs. That's where radar alerts and company invites show up.

If notifications are switched off, you'll see "Notifications are off" with a prompt to "Enable them in Settings to get radar alerts." Tap through to your phone's Settings and turn them on so you don't miss a load.


Screenshot
The notifications hub in the Numeo App
A product screenshot will be added here.

Choose where radar alerts land

Load Radar watches your saved searches and can reach you three ways:


Mobile push — a notification on your phone.

Telegram — alerts in your Telegram chat.

Email — alerts in your inbox.


Pick the channels that fit how you work when you set up a radar. Push notifications are delivered through Firebase, so make sure they're enabled in your phone's Settings.

Join the Numeo community on Telegram

Numeo Community isn't a screen inside the app — tapping it opens a Telegram group in the Telegram app. There's a group for each language, so you land in the one that matches your app language (the default group is t.me/numeoapp).

It's the place to swap notes with other dispatchers and drivers, ask questions, and hear about what's new. You'll need the Telegram app installed to join.

Searching loadsIntermediate
Keep a lane live with Auto Refresh
Refresh a hot lane by hand, or turn on Auto Refresh to re-scan every few seconds — new loads merge in without the board flashing.
2 min read

When a lane is hot, you want the newest loads the second they post. Load Hub gives you two ways to stay current: a manual refresh, and an Auto Refresh toggle that re-scans on its own.

Refresh by hand

Click "Refresh now" to re-run the current search immediately. New matches merge into the table you're already looking at.

Turn on Auto Refresh

Flip the "Auto Refresh" toggle and Load Hub keeps re-scanning the lane for you.


Set the average interval — anywhere from 5 to 30 seconds (it defaults to 8). Numeo spaces the refreshes out slightly so they don't all fire on the exact same beat.

A live countdown shows the seconds until the next scan.

New loads merge in rather than clearing and redrawing the whole board — so your place, your sort, and your selected rows hold while fresh loads slot in.


Toggle it back off any time to freeze the board where it is.


Animated demo
Auto Refresh re-scanning a lane with a live countdown
A short screen recording will be added here.

Good to know


Auto Refresh keeps one lane current while you're watching it. To cover a lane in the background and get alerted when a match posts — even with Load Hub closed — pair it with Load Radar, which watches your saved lanes and pings your phone or Telegram. Load Radar is on Numeo's paid plans; see the pricing page.

Your email signature and footer
Set one signature that rides on every broker email — a rich footer editor with your logo, shared across all your templates.
3 min read

Your signature is set once and added to every broker email you send from Numeo Spot. It's one footer per account — not per template — so you update it in one place and every email carries it.

Set your signature

Open the Templates tab in the side panel to find the footer editor.


Write your signature in the editor and format it the way you want.

Upload your logo so it shows in the footer.

Save it.


Until you add your own, the field shows the placeholder "Enter email footer/signature…". Once saved, your footer is appended to every broker email you send.


Screenshot
The signature and footer editor in the Templates tab

One signature, every template

The signature is shared across all your templates — the three template types all use the same footer. There's nothing to keep in sync per template. Change it once and every email, from any template, goes out with the new version.

Good to know


The signature rides on every send, including multi-broker bulk emails and emails sent from a chosen sender inbox.

Vetting brokers & loadsIntermediate
Blacklist brokers and MCs
Blacklist brokers you never want to work with — Spot flags their loads on the board, and Load Radar can skip their alerts.
2 min read

Some brokers you just don't want to deal with again — a bad experience, a No Buy, a lane that never works out. Numeo Spot gives you two ways to keep them out of your way: a broker blacklist that flags their loads right on the board, and a separate Load Radar filter that skips their alerts.

Blacklist a broker from the board

Open a broker's load and blacklist them in one tap. From then on, Spot flags that broker's loads on your DAT or Truckstop board — their rows carry a blacklist marker (a badge and a subtle border) so you spot them at a glance and steer clear. Un-blacklist them the same way.


It works on the broker, so the flag holds across lanes.

The blacklist is shared across your company — once someone marks a broker, your whole team sees the flag.



Screenshot
A blacklisted broker's row flagged on the board
A product screenshot will be added here.

Skip a broker's Load Radar alerts

Load Radar has its own Broker MC blacklist field. Type the MC numbers you never want alerts for, and Radar skips loads from those brokers — so a broker you've written off won't wake up your phone.

This is separate from the board blacklist above: the board flag marks brokers visually as you browse, while the Radar field suppresses notifications for the MC numbers you list.

Good to know


Both work on the broker's MC number, so they hold even if the broker posts different lanes.

Blacklisting is your own do-not-work list — to judge a broker you don't know yet, use factoring status and broker trust signals.

To hide loads by geography or numbers rather than by broker, use smart filters.

Get startedBeginner
Meet the AI Hub agents
The AI Hub agents in plain English — search, scoring, chat, email, outreach, the send gate, and voice — who does what and how they hand off.
4 min read

AI Hub isn't one big bot. Behind the board is a small team of agents, each with one job — find, rank, work the thread, book — passing a load down the line. You mostly talk to the chat; it brings in the rest. This is who does what, so you know what's happening when a load moves.

The team


Search agent — takes what you ask for, typed in plain English or filled into the form, and turns it into a real load-board search. This is the handoff line with search: it finds the candidates; everything else happens on top. See the search agent.

Scoring agent — ranks and tiers what comes back so the strongest loads float up. See how AI Hub ranks loads.

The chat (planning agent) — the assistant you actually talk to. For anything bigger than a quick answer, it plans the steps and drives the other agents' tools to get there. See Ask Numeo AI and the planning agent up close.

Email agent — works one broker thread on one load: figures out what the load still needs, asks for exactly that, and marks it ready when nothing's left. See the email agent.

Broker-outreach agent — runs a cold, multi-load thread with a broker ("got anything moving?"), sorts what they send back, and asks you which to chase. See broker outreach.

The send gate (classifier) — not a chatbot, a checkpoint. In the automated modes, it reads each outbound draft and decides: safe to send, or bring it back to you first. See how the send classifier works.

Voice — the same conversation, spoken. Money actions get a read-back and an explicit "yes" before anything happens. See voice mode.


How they hand off

A load moves down the line, and you stay in the loop at the points that matter:


You ask — typed or on the form.

The search agent runs the search; the scoring agent ranks what comes back.

You (or the chat) pick a load to work.

The email or broker-outreach agent runs the thread — asking for what's missing, framing the rate as a question.

The send gate checks each outbound message in the automated modes.

You hit Book It; the load turns Booked only after the broker confirms.


You're the one in charge

The agents do the repetitive first pass. They draft, rank, and line things up — but nothing outward-facing leaves without you in the automated modes, and in Manual mode you send every message yourself. Book It is always your call, and there's no auto-book. How much each agent does before it checks with you is set by your AI mode.

The same team backs AI Hub everywhere it runs: the web app, the Ask Numeo AI panel on your DAT board, and AI Dispatch in the mobile app. See what stays in your control.

Connecting sourcesIntermediate
Reconnect expired sources
Read the connected, expired, and not-connected source pills, and use the Reconnect dropdown to bring an expired broker or board back.
2 min read

Broker and board logins don't last forever — they time out. Load Hub shows you exactly which sources are connected, which have expired, and which were never set up, and gives you a one-click way to reconnect.

Reading the source pills

Every source in the source bar is a pill in one of three states:


Connected — a blue checkbox. It's working, and its loads show in your results.

Expired — an amber warning. It was connected, but the login timed out. Reconnect to bring it back.

Not connected — a plus-circle. Never set up. Connect it to add its loads.


The source bar header keeps a running count: "{n} selected broker(s)", and when some have dropped, "{n} disconnected broker(s)".


Screenshot
The source bar showing an expired pill and the Reconnect dropdown
A product screenshot will be added here.

Reconnect an expired source


When you have disconnected brokers, a "Reconnect" dropdown appears in the source bar. It lists each expired source with how long ago it dropped — "expired Xh/Xd ago".

Pick the source from the dropdown to reconnect it. Broker accounts reconnect through the extension; Sylectus reconnects through its login window.

Once it's back, the pill returns to a blue check and its loads flow into your results again.


Hover any pill to see its action — the tooltip reads Enable, Disable, Connect, or Reconnect for that source.

Good to know


Quick health check: any amber pill needs a reconnect before it'll return loads. If a lane looks light, scan the source bar first.

Mailbox & conversationsIntermediate
Send bids and counter offers
From a broker thread, send a bid, ask for the info you're missing, request the rate confirmation, and answer a broker's counter with your own.
3 min read

Negotiating a load in the app comes down to a few moves: put a number on it, ask for what you're missing, get the paperwork, and answer when the broker comes back with a different price. You do all of it from inside the broker thread, and every message stays on the load.

Send a bid

Open the broker thread for a load and tap "Send bid" to put your number on it. Your bid goes out from your connected mailbox and lands on the thread, so you always see what you offered and when.

New to threads? Start with Set up your mailbox and email brokers.

Ask for what you're missing

Before or during a negotiation you often need more than a price:


"Send info request" — ask the broker for the details you don't have yet.

"Request RC" — ask for the rate confirmation so you have the load in writing.


Both go out on the same thread, so the whole exchange for that load stays in one place.

Answer a counter

When the broker replies with a different number, tap "Counter ${amount}" to answer with yours. Each counter posts to the thread, so the back-and-forth reads top to bottom and you can always see where the rate stands.

Good to know


Everything stays on the load. Bids, info requests, RC requests, and counters all live in the per-load thread. See Manage conversations and invite a dispatcher.

Send faster with templates. Save your bid and info emails so a message goes out in a couple of taps. See Customize your email templates.

Let AI take the first pass. You can hand the outreach to Ask Numeo AI to find and book, which drafts the broker email and checks the broker before it sends.

Voice dispatchPower user
Voice languages and continuity
Switch the conversation language mid-call and pick up whatever the voice session found right in your chat thread.
3 min read

Voice dispatch speaks your language — literally. You can talk to Numeo in any of the app's supported languages, switch mid-call without hanging up, and the loads it finds carry straight over into your chat so nothing gets lost when the call ends.


Screenshot
Switching the conversation language during a voice call
A product screenshot will be added here.

Choose how Numeo talks to you

In a voice session you can set the language Numeo speaks and listens in. Look for "Choose how the AI communicates with you" and "Switch conversation language." Numeo speaks many of the app's languages, and falls back to English where the voice engine doesn't fully support a language yet.

Switch language mid-call

You don't have to end the call to change languages. Pick a new one from "Switch conversation language" and Numeo swaps its speech stack on the spot — it starts listening and answering in the new language right away. Handy when you switch from talking to a broker to talking to a driver, or want to hear a rate explained in your first language.

Voice results carry into your chat

A voice session isn't a dead end. As Numeo works, the loads and cards it finds land in your visible chat thread — the same thread you use for typed AI Dispatch. So when the call wraps with "Voice chat session ended," everything it surfaced is right there waiting: you can review the loads, open full details, and book or bid by tapping, exactly as if you'd typed the request.

This means you can start hands-free on the road and finish the booking by hand when you're parked — one continuous conversation, no re-searching.

Good to know


Captions match the language — the live transcript follows whichever language you're speaking, so you can read along in it too.

Same session, same thread — switching language keeps you in the same call and the same chat; you don't lose the loads already found.


Related

Ask Numeo AI to find and book loads — continue in the chat where your voice results land.

Change the app language — set the language for the whole app.

Filter loads by pay and distance — RPM ($/mi), Min Rate ($), Min Mi, and Max Mi.
2 min read

The second filter row trims your results down to loads that pay what you need and run the distance you want. Four fields do the work.

RPM ($/mi)

RPM ($/mi) sets a minimum rate per mile. Because it's normalized to distance, RPM is the fairest way to compare a short haul against a long one — set your floor and low-paying lanes drop out.

Min Rate ($)

Min Rate ($) sets a minimum total rate. Use it when you have a hard dollar number the load has to clear, regardless of miles.

Min Mi and Max Mi

Min Mi and Max Mi cap the loaded distance:


Min Mi — hide short hops when you want a longer run.

Max Mi — hide long hauls when you want to stay close.


Good to know


Rate, RPM, and Miles are all columns in the results table, and you can sort by rate or RPM to put the best-paying loads on top — see reading the results table and sort, reorder, and hide duplicates.

Rate and mileage are about the paid load; empty miles are handled separately by the deadhead filters.

Troubleshooting & FAQPower user
DAT not working
DAT returns no loads — check that you're on Ultra, have the Numeo extension installed, and are logged in at one.dat.com.
3 min read

DAT has three requirements the other sources don't. If DAT isn't returning loads, it's almost always one of them missing. Check them in this order.

1. Are you on Ultra?

DAT is an Ultra-gated source. On a lower plan, selecting DAT opens an upgrade prompt instead of adding the source. See plans, limits, and the company filter and the pricing page for what Ultra includes.

2. Is the extension installed?

DAT is extension-only — it won't run without the Numeo Chrome extension. If it's missing, Load Hub prompts you to install it first. See install the Numeo extension.

3. Are you logged in at one.dat.com?

DAT runs against your own DAT login. When you turn DAT on, Load Hub shows "Before searching DAT" — "Make sure you're ready in 2 steps":


"Open one.dat.com in your browser." Use the "Open DAT One" button.

"Make sure you're logged in to your DAT account."


Then choose "I'm already logged in." On each search, the extension opens one.dat.com in a background tab, uses your login, and streams matching loads back into your table.

Still empty?


If your DAT session logged out, sign back in at one.dat.com and search again — a dropped DAT session is the most common cause.

If the source pill turned amber, reconnect it — see a source expired or won't connect.

Full setup walkthrough: search DAT loads.

Call brokers with RingCentral
Connect RingCentral once to click-to-dial brokers from the board in your browser — no separate app — and see connection and blocked states.
3 min read

RingCentral is the deepest of Spot's calling options. Connect it once and you can click a broker's number to dial straight from the board — in your browser, with no separate app open.

Connect RingCentral


Open the Numeo Spot popup from the toolbar icon.

Go to the VoIP tab.

Sign in to RingCentral to link your account.


Once it's linked, the Ring Central Web option is ready whenever you're working a load.


Screenshot
The VoIP tab in the Numeo Spot popup
A product screenshot will be added here.

Click-to-dial from the board

With RingCentral connected, click a broker's number on a load and RingCentral places the call in your browser — no dialing by hand, no copying the number into another app. Choose Ring Central Web as your calling method and it dials for you every time.

Connection and blocked states

Spot shows you where the connection stands, so a call never fails silently:


Connected — RingCentral is linked and ready to dial.

Blocked or dropped — Spot flags it when the call is blocked or the link drops, so you know to reconnect from the VoIP tab instead of wondering why nothing dialed.


Good to know


RingCentral is one of several ways to call. You can also use plain Call (tel:), Google Voice, or Zoom — see Call the broker from the load board.

If the connection drops, reconnect from the popup's VoIP tab.

On the road (drivers)Intermediate
Read a driver load and your payout
The driver load screen shows equipment, your payout, route, hazmat, dispatcher notes, and the BOL and POD proof you need to capture.
3 min read

The driver load screen is the full picture of a run — what you're hauling, what you'll get paid, where you're going, and which documents you need to capture along the way. Open it before you accept a load and again while you're running it.


Screenshot
A driver load screen with the financial and route summary
A product screenshot will be added here.

Open a load

Tap any load — from Opportunities, from your trips, or from the ACTIVE TRIP card on your dashboard — to open its full detail screen. Everything below sits on that one screen.

Your payout and the numbers

The Financial & Route Summary is where the money lives:


Load Gross — the total on the load.

Total Rate — the rate for the run.

Your Payout — what lands with you.


Check Your Payout before you accept so there are no surprises. See Accept a load from Opportunities.

Equipment, route, and notes

The rest of the screen tells you how to run it:


Equipment & Reference — the equipment needed and the load's reference numbers.

Route Details — your stops and the miles between them.

Hazmat Details — any hazardous-material requirements, when they apply.

Dispatcher Notes — instructions your dispatcher left on the load.


Documents and proof

Under DOCUMENTS & PROOF, the load spells out exactly what to capture and when:


BOL required at pickup

POD required at delivery


Capture each one from the same load with the scanner and attach it to the right stop, so your dispatcher gets proof without asking. See Scan and upload documents.

Good to know


This is the Numeo Driver side of the app. What you see here is the driver's read of the load — payout, route, and proof.

The DOCUMENTS & PROOF checklist shows what's still missing at a glance, so you can see whether a run is fully documented before you close it out.
